sources.what_was_read: Read the full Zenodo API metadata, including MD5 checksums. Downloaded neurons.csv.gz (1.68 MB), classification.csv.gz (1.44 MB) and visual_neuron_types.csv.gz (0.25 MB) and inspected their headers and row counts. Matched file MD5s against the public Codex GCS bucket. The Seung and Matsliah papers were read as abstracts only (Europe PMC).

key_findings.finding: This is a first-party (H. S. Seung) CC-BY-4.0 copy of Codex v783 export files, downloadable without login. Its connections_no_threshold.csv.gz is byte-identical (MD5 8332c0f03acd2419f56f9bbc002a1554) to Codex GCS 783/connections_no_threshold.csv.gz and 783/connections_buhmann_no_threshold.csv.gz, so these are Buhmann-synapse edges. neurons.csv.gz is identical to Codex 783/neurons.csv.gz. classification.csv.gz and visual_neuron_types.csv.gz are older versions than the current Codex files.
key_findings.numbers: connections_no_threshold.csv.gz 212,093,967 B; neurons.csv.gz 1,679,884 B (139,255 rows); classification.csv.gz 1,438,155 B (139,255 rows); cell_stats.csv.gz 2,526,548 B; visual_neuron_types.csv.gz 248,706 B (47,521 rows)

key_findings.finding: Schemas, read from the files. Connections: pre_root_id, post_root_id, neuropil, syn_count, nt_type, one row per pair per neuropil, no threshold. Neurons: root_id, group, nt_type, nt_type_score, da/ser/gaba/glut/ach/oct _avg. Classification (Zenodo version): root_id, flow, super_class, class, sub_class, cell_type, hemibrain_type, hemilineage, side, nerve. Visual types: root_id, type, category, side.

Our own measurement on neurons.csv.gz (v783). 14.1% of neurons have a blank nt_type with score 0 and group 'NO_CONS', mostly optic (8,352) and sensory (8,123); the blank means no consensus, which is our inference. Median nt_type_score is 0.70, and 20.8% of neurons score <0.5. Known-transmitter optic types are often mis-signed: Dm9 (glutamatergic in the literature) is called ACH in 178 of 205 neurons; L1 GLUT 836 / GABA 323 / blank 608 of 1,775; Mi9 GLUT 1,020 / GABA 172 / blank 358 of 1,551; photoreceptors R1-6 (histaminergic, a class the classifier lacks) blank 4,366 / ACH 3,351 / GLUT 595 of 8,456.

sources.citation: Shiu PK, Sterne GR, Spiller N, Franconville R, Sandoval A, et al., Scott K. A Drosophila computational brain model reveals sensorimotor processing. Nature 634, 210-219 (2024). doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07763-9. PMC11446845. Code: github.com/philshiu/Drosophila_brain_model.
sources.what_was_read: Read the abstract, the feeding validation passages (MN9 screen), the grooming section, the Discussion limitations, the Methods on neurotransmitter assignment, robustness and grooming modelling, and the Data and Code availability. Not read: full taste-interaction results and the Supplementary tables. For the repo: README, LICENSE, file tree with sizes (GitHub API), model.py parameters, and the first 600 bytes of the Completeness CSVs.

key_findings.finding: A whole-brain LIF model in Brian2, built on FlyWire v630 (127,400 proofread neurons). Weights are synapse count × sign, with a single free parameter W_syn chosen so that sugar GRNs at 100 Hz give about 80% of maximal MN9 firing. A neuron is set inhibitory if more than half of its presynapses are predicted GABA or Glu; DA, 5-HT and OA neurons are set excitatory.
key_findings.numbers: v_th −45 mV, v_rest/reset −52 mV, τ_m 20 ms, τ_syn 5 ms, delay 1.8 ms, w_syn 0.275 mV; 30 trials of 1,000 ms each; about 5 min per 1,000 ms trial per CPU thread

key_findings.finding: Functional validation against independent experiments. Of the predictions the authors could test experimentally, 91% matched; excluding the unbalanced split-GAL4 screen, 84%. In an unbiased screen of 106 SEZ split-GAL4 cell types at 50 Hz, 11 were predicted to activate MN9 and 10 of those 11 drove rostrum extension; of the 95 predicted not to, 4 did. Shuffled weights activated MN9 in only 1 of 100 simulations. JO-CE neurons drive aBN1 but JO-F neurons do not, confirmed by calcium imaging.
key_findings.numbers: 91% of 164 predictions; 84% excluding the screen; 10/11 true positives; 4/95 false negatives; 1/100 shuffled

key_findings.finding: Sensitivity to assumptions. Making glutamate excitatory removes the inhibitory bitter/Ir94e result and raises the screen's false-positive rate. W_syn ±30% and the inhibitory weight ±50% change little.
key_findings.numbers: false-positive rate 1% → 16% with excitatory glutamate; accuracy 91% → 88-89% under the inhibitory-weight change

key_findings.finding: Repo contents: MIT licence ('Copyright (c) 2023 Philip Shiu and Nico Spiller'), with derived FlyWire data bundled. Connectivity parquet columns include Presynaptic_Index, Postsynaptic_Index and 'Excitatory x Connectivity'. Completeness CSVs have columns root_id and Completed. GitHub raw supports byte ranges (Accept-Ranges: bytes).
key_findings.numbers: Connectivity_783.parquet 100,804,642 B; Completeness_783.csv 3,327,347 B; 2023_03_23_connectivity_630_final.parquet 86,630,944 B; 2023_03_23_completeness_630_final.csv 3,057,611 B

sources.validation_design: Model predictions (neurons that respond, are sufficient or are necessary for MN9/aDN activity) were compared with independent optogenetic activation and silencing, calcium imaging and behavioural PER experiments, partly from earlier work by the same lab (Shiu, Sterne et al.) and partly new (the split-GAL4 screen; JO-F→aBN1). The single free parameter was fitted on sugar→MN9. A weight-shuffle control was run. Readouts were not retrained per held-out task, but the stimulation rate was swept from 10 to 200 Hz.
stated_limitations: Zero basal firing, so inhibition of silent neurons has no effect
No gap junctions, neuromodulation, neuropeptides, morphology or receptor dynamics
Accuracy is limited by the synapse and neurotransmitter predictions
Glutamate sign assumed inhibitory
Absolute firing rates are not trustworthy
Fails for inhibitory or neuromodulatory screen hits (Tentacular, Phantom, Usnea)
Descending circuits are incomplete in the brain-only volume
sources.code: MIT (GitHub API and LICENSE file checked). Python with Brian2. CPU-feasible; a Colab notebook is provided. Raw model outputs: Edmond archive doi:10.17617/3.CZODIW (size unverified).
sources.data: The bundled derived connectivity for 630 and 783 is downloadable anonymously from GitHub (about 101 MB, above our 5 MB Gate-1 cap, so not downloaded). The licence of the bundled data is ambiguous: MIT repo versus the FlyWire CC BY-NC/CC-BY terms.
sources.novelty_threat_for_m08: This strongly pre-empts any M08 claim that 'a structure-only (connectome+NT) model predicts feeding or antennal-grooming circuit function' (G-FUNCTION in these circuits). It also already provides the weight-shuffle baseline. An M08 function result in these circuits would at best be a reproduction unless the circuit is generated from compact rules.
sources.gaps_m08_could_test: (1) A test the authors did not run: replace the real SEZ subcircuit with a circuit generated from compact rules (type-level SBM, geometry+type, hemilineage), keep the frozen LIF and W_syn, and check whether Shiu's experimentally validated predictions survive. This tests whether 'rule-generated structure suffices for function' (G-STRUCT→G-FUNCTION). (2) Use the 164 empirical outcomes (Supplementary Table 9) as a frozen functional benchmark. (3) Port to v783 and the flywire_annotations v3.2.0 GRN retyping. The release warns that the old 'sugar/water' sub-class also contained water (LB3a) and aversive (LB3d) neurons, which could change which GRNs are stimulated. (4) Treat the glutamate sign as an explicit uncertainty dimension.

sources.citation: Eckstein N, Bates AS, Champion A, Du M, Yin Y, Schlegel P, et al., Jefferis GSXE, Funke J. Neurotransmitter classification from electron microscopy images at synaptic sites in Drosophila melanogaster. Cell 187(10):2574-2594 (2024). doi:10.1016/j.cell.2024.03.016. PMC11106717. Supplemental data: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.10593546.
sources.what_was_read: Read the abstract, the accuracy results, the misprediction paragraphs, the Limitations of the study, the STAR Methods passages on neuron-level confidence and on optic-lobe and monoamine mispredictions, and the Lacin's-law results. Zenodo 10593546 was read as metadata only.

key_findings.finding: Six-class transmitter classifier trained from EM images, with a neuron split for testing. On FAFB the test set was 40,104 presynapses from 185 held-out neurons; per-neuron accuracy is a majority vote over neurons with >30 presynapses. Accuracy stays high under neuropil and hemilineage splits.
key_findings.numbers: FAFB 87% per synapse / 94% per neuron; HemiBrain 78% / 91%; known cell types 91%

key_findings.finding: Accuracy on known cell types (FAFB-FlyWire) varies by class; serotonin is least reliable. Optic lobe: 96% of about 29,000 cholinergic, 87% of about 3,600 GABAergic and 91% of about 1,600 glutamatergic neurons were correct. However, about 5,700 neurons of glutamatergic types (L1, Dm1, Dm3, Dm4, Dm11, Dm12) were predicted only 61% Glu and 30% GABA. Dm9 was predicted Glu in only 3% of cells, Mi1 ACh in 67%, and 114 photoreceptors (R1-8, histaminergic) were predicted octopamine.

Not predicted at all: histamine, tyramine, glycine, nitric oxide, about 53 neuropeptides, co-transmission, receptor expression and gap junctions. A neuron is labelled uncertain if its top two transmitters differ by <10%.
Lacin's law (each hemilineage expresses one fast transmitter) holds in most hemilineages. The exceptions look like discrete developmental switches correlated with morphology.
key_findings.numbers: 88% of hemilineages

sources.validation_design: Held-out neurons (neuron split), plus alternative neuropil and hemilineage splits. Comparison with literature ground truth for 356 cell types from 21 studies. Cross-dataset agreement: 95% of 2,626 matched cell types agree between FAFB-FlyWire and the hemibrain.
stated_limitations: Mispredictions concentrate in co-transmitting neurons
Transmitters outside the 6 classes are not modelled
Serotonin is poorly predicted
Sign is not fully determined by the transmitter (glutamate and GABA receptors vary)
The optic lobe was largely absent from the ground truth

sources.novelty_threat_for_m08: Lacin's law is a published compact developmental rule (hemilineage → single fast transmitter). M08 cannot claim it as a discovery.
sources.gaps_m08_could_test: Make the edge sign an explicit latent variable with Eckstein's confusion matrix as a prior, rather than a fixed ±1. Test whether M08 conclusions survive sign resampling. For the motion pathway, override L1, Mi9, Dm9 and photoreceptor signs from the literature or curated tables and report both versions.

key_findings.finding: fafbseg connectivity and synapse queries go through CAVEclient with an auth token. The dataset 'public' maps to datastack flywire_fafb_public; 'flat_783' and 'flat_630' also map to it, with the flat segmentation at precomputed://gs://flywire_v141_m783. The setup doc requires generating a token at global.daf-apis.com after logging in. Annotations, by contrast, are pulled from GitHub without a token.

The FlyConnectome CAVE tutorial says every user must create a CAVE account (Google account required) and a token. FlyWire data is public in the sense that no extra permissions are needed beyond the account.

sources.citation: Lappalainen JK, Tschopp FD, Prakhya S, McGill M, Nern A, Shinomiya K, Takemura S, Gruntman E, Macke JH, Turaga SC. Connectome-constrained networks predict neural activity across the fly visual system. Nature 634, 1132-1140 (2024). doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07939-3. PMC11525180.
sources.what_was_read: Read only the abstract, the opening Results paragraphs, and the Methods section on constructing the connectome. The purpose was to confirm which connectome was used.

key_findings.finding: The deep mechanistic network (DMN) connectome was NOT built from FlyWire. It was built from Janelia FIB-25 (7 medulla columns) and FIB-19 (optic lobe) data, blended into a spatially invariant column model with an EM column-assignment algorithm.
key_findings.numbers: 1,801 neurons (702 FIB-25, 1,099 FIB-19); about 830 hand-annotated reference columns; 64 identified cell types compared with measurements; ensemble of 50 models

key_findings.finding: The paper reports that, with measurements of connectivity alone, sparser networks give much better activity predictions (synthetic MNIST test).
key_findings.numbers: median Pearson correlation 0.85 at 10% connectivity versus 0.38 at 80%

sources.validation_design: Predicted cell-type tuning (no activity data used in training) compared with published recordings. Details not read.
stated_limitations: Not read in detail (handled by another Gate-1 source review)
sources.novelty_threat_for_m08: Pre-empts claims that 'connectome + task optimisation predicts motion-pathway tuning'.
sources.gaps_m08_could_test: FlyWire provides independent optic-lobe connectomes from a different animal and EM modality: both eyes, plus MAOL. Fitting a compact columnar/type rule on one source and testing on FlyWire right, FlyWire left (excluding the damaged lamina) or MAOL is a genuine cross-individual test. Whether someone has already run flyvis on FlyWire is unverified.

sources.citation: Third-party 2026 Zenodo deposits found while searching 'flywire' (not peer reviewed, not vetted). Examples: Correig-Fraga, Guimerà, Sales-Pardo, 'Structure alone supports efficient visual computation in the Drosophila visual system' data record (doi:10.5281/zenodo.21549559, CC-BY-4.0); Wilson J, 'WireType, FAFB & MCNS outputs' (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23325190, CC-BY-NC-4.0); 'Neurotransmitter prediction confidence for 126,419 FlyWire neurons, corrected for the spatial clustering of synapses' (doi:10.5281/zenodo.22795740); Wang Y, 'Packaging choices change connectome-simulation outcomes' (doi:10.5281/zenodo.22998484); Liu H et al., 'Neuronal birth order leaves a reproducible trace in the geometry of three Drosophila connectomes' (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23497175).
sources.what_was_read: Read the Zenodo metadata descriptions only, plus the README of 21549559. Many other 2026 'flywire' deposits look like low-quality or AI-generated preprints and were ignored.

key_findings.finding: Several groups in 2026 posted (unreviewed) work on themes that overlap M08. Topics: structure-only visual computation tested against randomized graphs (derived from Zenodo 10676866 and flywire_annotations v2.1.0); predicting the transmitter from connectivity across FAFB and MCNS (weighted F1 0.913 on FAFB); the effective number of independent observations behind NT confidence, which the deposit reports at about 10× fewer than the published confidence score assumes; the dependence of LIF simulation outcomes on the glutamate-sign convention; birth-order and site-of-addition rules across MCNS, FlyWire and BANC.
key_findings.numbers: as stated in the deposit metadata; not verified

unverified_items: Exact contents, sizes and citation-requirement text of the Codex download portal (codex.flywire.ai/api/download): it sits behind Google sign-in plus an api_token and was not accessed.

Which synapse table Codex currently uses by default for FAFB downloads and statistics, and what the 'Yu et al.' synapse-detection method is. The Codex About page names 'Yu et al.' and says pre-July-2025 releases used Buhmann et al., but no paper for Yu et al. was found. That the 'princeton' files (2025-07-08) are this new set is our inference.
What Codex's '3,732,460 connections' for FAFB v783 counts (pairs, pair×neuropil rows, or Princeton synapses). The paper reports 2,700,513 connections with ≥5 synapses.

Licence status of the public GCS bucket gs://flywire-data/codex/data/: no licence or terms found there, and its use is not documented as sanctioned (it appears only in Codex's Apache-2.0 loader code).

Licence conflict: FlyWire Principles say published data are CC BY-NC 4.0; Zenodo deposits by the FlyWire Consortium, Schlegel and Seung are tagged CC-BY-4.0; flywire_annotations on GitHub has no LICENSE file. The Citation Guidelines Google Doc was not read.
That connections_olr_min_2.csv.gz is exactly 'right optic lobe, ≥2 synapses', inferred from the neuropil values in the first 128 KB only.
Release date of FlyWire 630. The Shiu filename suggests a 2023-03-23 export, and Dorkenwald calls 783 the second public release, but no exact public-release date for 630 was found.

Whether Shiu's Connectivity_783.parquet row groups are laid out so that HTTP byte-range reads of only a sub-circuit are possible. GitHub raw advertises Accept-Ranges, but the parquet layout was not inspected. Zenodo did not advertise Accept-Ranges in our HEAD request.
Size and licence of Shiu's model-output archive (Edmond doi:10.17617/3.CZODIW).
BANC (v626/v888) publication details, licence and download terms; seen only in Codex, secondary web search and Zenodo metadata (e.g. BANC-project, bancr deposits by Bates et al. 2026).
MCNS, MAOL and MANC download terms and licences (Codex FAQ says to use the project homepages; not checked).
Whether flyvis or other groups have already run Lappalainen-style models on FlyWire or MAOL optic lobes.

Mapping of Shiu's grooming neurons (aBN1, aBN2, aDN1, aDN2) and JON subclasses to current 783 root IDs and annotation names, given the JO retyping in flywire_annotations v3.1.0. Only 1 aBN1 label and no exact aBN2, aDN1 or aDN2 labels were found in Codex labels.csv.
Content of Tastekin et al. Cell 2026 (complete gustatory connectome) and Berg et al. Cell 2026 (MaleCNS): known only from the flywire_annotations README and changelog.

Our NT statistics come from Codex neurons.csv (nt_type, nt_type_score). Whether these are computed exactly like Eckstein's neuron-level calls or flywire_annotations top_nt/top_nt_conf is unverified. That blank nt_type/'NO_CONS' means 'no consensus or too few presynapses' is our inference.
Seung 2024 and Matsliah 2024 were read as abstracts only; their validation designs are not summarized here.

Dorkenwald Supplementary Fig. 2 (per-neuropil attachment rates) was not read. We used Codex's neuropil_stats.csv and synapse_attachment_rates.csv.gz instead, which may correspond to a different synapse set or date.
All 2026 third-party Zenodo deposits listed are unvetted; their numbers are as stated in metadata only.
read:flywire.summary_for_m08:
FlyWire Gate-1 data-access summary, prepared without signing in or using any token. We downloaded only files under 5 MB, plus HEAD requests and 64-128 KB byte-range reads of larger files. Working copies (paper texts and small CSVs) are under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-null3351-Code-neural-primitive-research/67758993-59ff-487e-8108-e1cc3e5b2603/scratchpad/flywire/. Nothing was written to the repository.

1) RELEASES. 630 is the first public release (Shiu et al. used it: 127,400 neurons). 783 is the second public release and the basis of all 2024 papers (139,255 neurons). Codex now offers only FAFB v783, plus other datasets: BANC v888 and v626 (a second female, brain plus nerve cord), MANC, MAOL (male right optic lobe) and MCNS (male CNS). Caveat: 'v783' is not one fixed dataset. Codex says it switched to a new synapse set ('Yu et al.', July 2025). The public bucket has both the Buhmann files (connections_buhmann* = connections* = the Zenodo/Seung files, MD5-verified) and the 'princeton' files (connections_princeton*, fafb_v783_princeton_synapse_table 2.7 GB). The flywire_annotations versions drift too: v2.1.0 matches the papers; v3.0-3.2 brings MaleCNS cross-checks, JO retyping and GRN retyping. Any M08 result must pin the file, synapse generation, annotation tag and checksum.

2) FILES AND NO-SIGN-IN ACCESS. Codex's portal requires Google sign-in plus an api_token, so the agent cannot use it. Copies reachable with no login:
(a) Zenodo 10676866, FlyWire Consortium, CC-BY-4.0 metadata, v783 only: proofread_connections_783.feather (852 MB; pair × neuropil syn_count with mean NT probabilities); flywire_synapses_783.feather (9.49 GB; all about 130M synapses with pre/post coordinates and per-synapse NT probabilities); per-neuron neuropil pre/post counts (16.9 MB and 234 MB); proofread_root_ids_783.npy (1.1 MB).
(b) Zenodo 17030629, H. S. Seung, CC-BY-4.0: a byte-identical Codex v783 connections_no_threshold.csv.gz (212 MB; columns pre_root_id, post_root_id, neuropil, syn_count, nt_type), neurons.csv.gz (1.68 MB; per-neuron NT prediction and score), cell_stats, plus older classification and visual_neuron_types.
(c) Zenodo 10877326, Schlegel, CC-BY-4.0: skeletons (5.36 GB) and NBLAST tables.
(d) Zenodo 12588557: information-flow ranks, about 1.5 MB each.
(e) Zenodo 10593546, Eckstein: synapse-level NT predictions, 7.7 GB.
(f) GitHub flywire_annotations: 31.7 MB TSV with hierarchical types, hemilineages and top_nt; no LICENSE file on GitHub, Zenodo mirror tagged CC-BY.
(g) GitHub philshiu/Drosophila_brain_model, MIT: Connectivity_783.parquet (100.8 MB), Completeness_783.csv (3.3 MB), and the 630 equivalents.
(h) The public GCS bucket used by Codex's own open-source loader, storage.googleapis.com/flywire-data/codex/data/fafb/{630,783}/, anonymously listable. It holds every Codex export, including small ones useful for circuit selection: classification (0.93 MB), consolidated_cell_types (0.90 MB), labels (4.8 MB), column_assignment (0.46 MB; hexagonal column x, y, p, q per columnar neuron), neuropil_synapse_table (4.7 MB), synapse_attachment_rates (3 KB), and a pre-cut right-optic-lobe edge list connections_olr_min_2 (27.5 MB; inferred). No licence is stated on the bucket. It also contains pickle files that must never be loaded.
fafbseg-py and CAVEclient need a token for connectivity; fafbseg annotations do not.

LICENCE. The articles are CC BY 4.0, and the Zenodo deposits say CC-BY-4.0. However, the FlyWire Principles say 'Published versions of FlyWire’s data are available under CC BY-NC 4.0', and the Terms of Service put community edits and annotations under CC-BY-NC 4.0. Recommendation: treat the data as CC BY-NC 4.0, cite Dorkenwald 2024 + Schlegel 2024 (plus Matsliah 2024, Berg 2026 and Tastekin 2026 if using annotations ≥3.2.0), and prefer the CC-BY Zenodo copies over the bucket.

3) EXTRACTING A SMALL CIRCUIT WITHOUT THE WHOLE BRAIN. Step 1: select root IDs from small annotation files (<5 MB).
- Motion pathway: consolidated types give, across both eyes, T4a-d 1,457-1,710 cells per subtype, T5a-d 1,469-1,536, Mi1 1,581, Tm3 1,756, Mi4 1,532, Mi9 1,551, Tm1/2/4/9 about 1,500 each, L1-L3, HS (6), VS1-8 (16), LPLC2 (210). column_assignment supplies retinotopic columns.
- Feeding: GRN subclasses in Codex classification (gustatory 334 plus 74 ascending; old 'sugar/water' 129, bitter 65). Shiu's named neurons (MN9, Fdg, Zorro, Clavicle, Phantom, Usnea, etc.) exist only as community labels.
- Grooming: JO labels (JO-C 113, JO-E 275, JO-F 172 labelled IDs); aBN1, aBN2, aDN1 and aDN2 need mapping from Shiu's tables or annotation synonyms.
Step 2: obtain edges. Options:
(i) Right optic lobe only: connections_olr_min_2 (27.5 MB).
(ii) Stream-filter the 212 MB CC-BY edge list on the fly. The bytes are still whole-brain, so this needs an explicit Gate-3 justification under the brief's ban on unnecessary whole-brain downloads.
(iii) Try HTTP range-reads of Shiu's parquet (feasibility unverified).
(iv) Ask the user to sign in to Codex themselves and export the query's connectivity CSV, or run CAVE with their own token.
Per-neuropil splits mean an optic-lobe or SEZ subgraph can also be cut by neuropil (ME/LO/LOP/LA for motion; GNG/PRW/SAD/AMMC for feeding and grooming).

4) CAVEATS THAT MATTER FOR MODELS.
- Synapses are machine-detected and unproofread (training ground truth from the calyx only; sensory neurons worse).
- Pre-attachment is 93.7% but post-attachment only 44.7%, varying by neuropil (e.g. AL_L post 0.54, AME_L 0.40). Weak edges are undercounted; the paper uses a ≥5 threshold, and Matsliah used ≥2 in the optic lobe.
- The left lamina is partially severed; there are no gap junctions; afferents are truncated; the FAFB imagery is left-right mirrored.
- Schlegel's reliability: >10-synapse edges are >90% reproducible across hemispheres and brains; only 16% of edges pass, but they carry 79% of synapses. About 53% of hemibrain edges reappear in FlyWire, and edge-weight differences ≤30% can be purely technical (precision 0.72, recall 0.77). These numbers set the realistic ceiling and null for any structure-prediction metric.
- NT predictions: 87% per synapse, 94% per neuron, 5-HT 33%; no histamine, glycine, tyramine, peptides or co-transmission. In Codex v783 (our measurement): 14.1% of neurons have no NT call, the median score is 0.70, and 20.8% score <0.5.
- Motion-pathway signs are unreliable: Dm9 called ACh in 178 of 205 cells (true: Glu); L1 Glu/GABA/blank mixed; Mi9 partly GABA or blank; photoreceptors (histaminergic) called ACh/Glu/blank. Shiu showed that switching glutamate to excitatory changes results (false positives 1% → 16%).

5) IMPLICATIONS FOR M08.
- Already pre-empted: structure-only LIF prediction of feeding and grooming function (Shiu: 91% of 164 tests; 1/100 shuffled-weight control); motion tuning from connectome + task (Lappalainen; which used Janelia FIB-19/25, not FlyWire); type-level compression and a 'genomic bottleneck' argument plus edge-reliability heuristics (Schlegel; not tested as a generator); Lacin's law (hemilineage → one fast transmitter in 88% of hemilineages); KC K-compensation (Schlegel).
- Open tests M08 could run:
  (1) Build the compact type/space/hemilineage generator Schlegel only describes. Score it on held-out hemispheres or brains (FlyWire L/R are correlated, so the stronger tests are hemibrain, BANC, MCNS and MAOL; their access terms are unverified) against the inter-individual ceiling.
  (2) Substitute a rule-generated SEZ circuit into the frozen Shiu model and test whether its validated predictions survive. This is a genuine G-STRUCT → G-FUNCTION test.
  (3) Test whether rules fitted on one optic lobe transfer to the other optic lobe and MAOL using column_assignment.
  (4) Treat synapse generation (Buhmann vs Princeton), threshold and NT sign as preregistered perturbation axes.
- Drosophila FlyWire offers no developmental time series. Hemilineage and birth order are only developmental proxies, so stage generalization must come from the C. elegans line.
- Gate-1 verdict for this line: a lawful, no-sign-in, real-circuit data subset exists, with independent functional validation outcomes (Shiu) and independent individuals available. Every file large enough to hold a whole-circuit edge list exceeds the 5 MB Gate-1 cap and needs a Gate-3 download decision.

sources.citation: Richter O., Schneidman E. (2025). Building the connectome of a small brain with a simple stochastic developmental generative model. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 122(47):e2504913122. doi:10.1073/pnas.2504913122. PMCID PMC12664000, PMID 41252150. Received 17 Mar 2025, accepted 16 Sep 2025, published online 18 Nov 2025 (issue 25 Nov 2025). Edited by Eve Marder. Licence CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (stated on the PMC page).
sources.what_was_read: I read the whole PMC main text: significance, abstract, introduction, all Results sections, every figure legend (Figs 1-7), Discussion, Materials and Methods (a short paragraph that points to the SI), data availability and the full 52-item reference list. The SI Appendix (pnas.2504913122.sapp.pdf, listed as 915.2 KB) could not be reached. PMC serves a proof-of-work 'Preparing to download' page, which I did not try to solve. PNAS returns a Cloudflare 403. The Europe PMC supplementary zip is over 5 MB (details under unverified items). As a proxy for the SI I used the bioRxiv v1 Methods and the SI figure legends (separate entry). I also read the code to see what was done in practice (repository entry).

key_findings.finding: Single-epoch developmental model with the 13 Cook et al. 2019 functional types. Trained on Witvliet adult worm 7 and tested on the whole adult worm 8 connectome. The authors say this matches non-developmental generative models of the adult worm (their ref 23, Haber et al. 2023).
key_findings.numbers: AUROC = 0.78 on test worm 8 (Fig 1G)

key_findings.finding: Ablations. Models using only birth time, or only distance, do better than chance. AUROC rises with the number of cell types: 1 < 3 (sensory/motor/inter) < 13 Cook types. Random type assignments are used as a control (Fig 2G).
key_findings.numbers: The text gives no AUROC values for the birth-time-only, distance-only, 1-type or 3-type models (figure-only, unverified)

key_findings.finding: Types inferred by greedy agglomerative clustering on worm 7 beat the 13 Cook types and need fewer types. 4 inferred types roughly match 13 Cook types. AUROC rises quickly up to about 10 types and changes little beyond 25. The authors choose 8 types, where AUROC passes 0.8.
key_findings.numbers: 8 inferred types: AUROC 0.81 (full model, Fig 5 text); 4 inferred ≈ 13 Cook types

key_findings.finding: Overfitting control (SI Fig S3B; method from the preprint). Models with 1-15 types were fitted to synthetic samples of an 8-type model. On those, AUROC peaks at 8 types. On real data AUROC keeps rising past 8, which the authors read as evidence that 8 types do not overfit.
Robustness to birth-time noise. Perturbing neuronal birth times by up to 50% barely changes synapse-level accuracy or whole-graph likelihood (SI Fig S2).
key_findings.numbers: 10 noise levels from 0.1 to 1.0, 100 repeats each (method detail from the preprint)

key_findings.finding: Structural statistics compared against held-out worm 8 (the code confirms Dataset8 is the comparison). In- and out-degree distributions fall within 2 SD of the model for almost all values. Most individual neuron degrees fall within 1 SD. Histograms of distances and of maximal birth times between connected pairs are reproduced, although the model was not trained on them.

The independent-synapse model gets reciprocity and triads wrong. Adding a reciprocity factor gamma (gamma = 7, chosen so reciprocity matches worm 7) fixes most triad frequencies and leaves AUROC unchanged.
key_findings.numbers: Erdős-Rényi reciprocity ≈ density² ≈ 0.0036. Observed reciprocity is ~4.5x the ER value; the 8-type independent model gives ~1.7x. Triad Jensen-Shannon divergence falls from 0.01135 to 0.00045 bits.

key_findings.finding: Compression by quantizing S+. Accuracy saturates at 14 parameters, about 5-fold smaller than the full 8-type model. The authors take this to mean the parameters are not fine-tuned.
key_findings.numbers: A 9-parameter model (7 S+ levels + S- + beta0, per the Fig 5B legend) reaches AUROC 0.77, 95% of the full model's 0.81, over ~30K potential synapses

key_findings.finding: Our reading of the code: the compressed-model search compares candidates by AUROC on test worm 8. So the compression level that keeps 95% of AUROC (Figs 5B and 5D) was chosen on the test individual. A param count of 66 for the full 8-type model (64 S+ + S- + beta0) is our arithmetic and fits the stated ~5-fold compression to 14.

Developmental trajectory, comparing one epoch with three epochs (S+ re-fitted per epoch), using 20 random half-splits of the dyads. Both reach similar adult test ROC curves. The single-epoch model's network density is far from the measured values at several stages, while the 3-epoch model follows them. The 3-epoch model wins on test log-likelihood ratio by a large margin early in development. Pruning (S- > 0) improves the multi-epoch fit compared with no pruning (Fig 6F).
key_findings.numbers: 20 splits. The text gives no adult-test AUROC for either model and no log-likelihood ratio magnitudes (unverified).

key_findings.finding: Backbone and variability. Worm 8 has 1,933 connections. 1,279 are shared with worm 7 and 863 with both worm 7 and the WormAtlas/White adult, which caps the shared backbone at about 45% of one worm's connections. The model gives higher probabilities to connections found in more datasets. Every connection predicted at p ≈ 1 appears in all 3 datasets, and these carry at least 13.5 synapses on average. Model probability correlates with mean synapse count across worms 7 and 8.
key_findings.numbers: Pearson r = 0.35, P < 1e-16 (Fig 7G)

key_findings.finding: Potential leakage in the backbone analysis (our reading of the code). The 8 types used in the split-half and backbone analyses were inferred from worm 7's full adjacency matrix, test-half dyads included, and worm 7 is one of the three datasets used for the 'appears in k datasets' grouping. Separately, the r = 0.35 in Fig 7G pools train-half and test-half dyad probabilities from a single split (split 16).

Overlap between model draws and the data at each developmental stage falls within 1 SD of the overlap between two model draws (SI Fig S9A). The authors add that the model is probably more variable than real worms are.

No neural activity, behaviour, function, perturbation or lesion prediction, gap junctions, other species, or male connectome is tested. Function appears only as future work in the Discussion. Only one cross-individual pair is tested (worm 7 to worm 8, same lab and stage), with no confidence intervals and no AUPRC or calibration.

sources.model_or_method_spec: Inputs fixed from outside sources (not fitted). (1) Neuron birth times: Pathak, Chatterjee & Sinha 2020 PLoS Comput Biol (ref 40). (2) 3D soma positions: Skuhersky et al. 2022 BMC Bioinformatics atlas (ref 41), adult coordinates normalized by 800 µm and held constant through development. (3) Worm elongation: a piecewise-linear length curve from Byerly et al. 1976 (ref 39); the code constants give 50 µm at t=0, 250 µm at hatching (800 min), 370/500/635 µm at hatching +12/+20/+28 h, and 800 µm at adult (3500 min), for 16-fold elongation in total. (4) Neuron types, one of: Cook et al. 2019 categories (1 type, 3 coarse types, or 13 of 15 subtypes present in the nerve ring); random partitions; or authors' 'inferred' types from greedy agglomerative clustering of the training worm's adjacency, merging the pair that least lowers an SBM 'hit rate' (expected agreement when a block-ER graph is sampled with per-block counts matching the data). That makes inferred types a stochastic-block-model fit to worm 7, not independent biology. (5) Connectomes: Witvliet et al. 2021 (ref 16), 8 animals across 7 stages, 180 nerve-ring neurons, chemical synapses only, binarized, autapses removed. For the backbone analysis, the WormAtlas adult (White 1986 / Chen 2006 / Varshney 2011, refs 47-49) is added. Generative process, in 10-min steps: a neuron appears at its birth time. At each step every absent ordered pair (i,j) forms with probability S+[tau_i,tau_j]·exp(-beta_t·d_ij), where beta_t = beta0·L(t)/L(0). Every existing synapse is pruned with a constant, type-independent S-. In the reciprocal variant the formation probability is min(gamma·S+·exp(-beta_t d), 1) when j->i already exists. Exact marginals come from the recurrence p_n = c_n + (1 - S- - c_n)·p_{n-1}; the reciprocal model tracks a 4-state dyad recurrence. Fitting: S- and beta0 by maximum likelihood over a 40x40 grid; the preprint states the range as [0, 0.05), and the exact PNAS grid is unverified. For each grid point, every S+ is set by binary search so the expected per-type-pair synapse count matches the training connectome (tolerance 0.05 synapses). Gamma is fixed per model: values 2-9 were scanned and gamma = 7 chosen because it reproduces worm 7's reciprocity. Multi-epoch variant: separate S+ per epoch, with epoch boundaries at the ages of Witvliet dataset 2 (5 h after hatching) and dataset 6 (27 h). Fitting is sequential, matching counts in the train halves of datasets 2, 6 and 8, with likelihood on the dataset 8 train half. Parameter counts (our arithmetic): 8-type single epoch = 66 (+gamma); 3-epoch = 194 (+gamma). These counts leave out the 180 type labels (about 540 bits at 8 types) and the 180 positions and 180 birth times.
sources.validation_design: (a) Cross-individual: train on the full worm 7 adult connectome (Witvliet Dataset7) and test on the full worm 8 (Dataset8). Both are adults from the same lab and pipeline. Types were inferred and gamma was chosen on worm 7. Metrics are AUROC with the diagonal removed, except in the compression figure code, plus degree, distance and birth-time histograms and triad distributions against worm 8. The reverse direction (8 to 7) is not reported, and AUROC has no CI or bootstrap. (b) Within-individual and developmental: 20 random splits of unordered neuron pairs into halves, the same split applied to every stage. Training uses the train halves of datasets 2, 6 and 8; testing uses the test halves of all stages (datasets 1-6 and 8). Stages 1, 3, 4 and 5 are never used in training, so those test points are interpolation between stages, but they are judged only by density trajectory and log-likelihood ratio, not by per-stage AUROC. No test holds out a whole stage or a whole individual for the developmental model. (c) Backbone: probabilities on the test-half dyads from the 3-epoch models, grouped by how many of worm 7, worm 8 and WormAtlas contain the connection; Pearson correlation with mean synapse count. (d) Controls: random types, an overfitting check on synthetic samples, birth-time noise, a no-pruning ablation, and single-epoch vs 3-epoch. No strong external baseline is run on the same split: no published generative model, no plain SBM or degree-corrected SBM, and no copy-the-other-worm baseline. The agreement with Haber et al. 2023 is asserted by quoting a similar AUROC.
stated_limitations: Each developmental stage comes from a different animal, so the assumed developmental 'path' through them may not be biologically realizable. Following one animal's connectome through development is beyond current experimental ability.

Only two developmental ingredients are modelled (lineage birth times and body elongation). Molecular, cellular and circuit-level developmental data could change the conclusions about how many epochs are needed.

The real wiring rules may differ from the model's. The model is a 'draft' of construction rules that still needs experimental verification, or the identification of other features that implement equivalent rules.

The model is probably more variable than real worms, and it lacks features that would reduce that variability. More connectomes are needed to estimate natural variability and give the comparisons statistical power.
There are too few connectomes to train on many individuals and test on others, so the authors fall back on indirect measures.
Type inference is a heuristic greedy clustering, so a more compact or better set of types may exist.
The independent-synapse model misses reciprocity and triad statistics (addressed with gamma).
Links to function, neural activity, behaviour and sexual dimorphism are left as future work.
sources.code: https://github.com/schneidmanlab/BrainBuildingPaper (cited as ref 52, 'deposited 14 August 2025'). No licence: the GitHub API reports license=null and /license returns 404 (checked 2026-10-25). Python 3.9, developed on Windows 10. Grid searches need an IBM LSF cluster. Details in the repository entry.
sources.data: All inputs come from previously published sources (refs 15, 16, 39-41, 47-49). Processed copies are bundled in the GitHub repository (CElegansData/), downloadable from raw.githubusercontent.com without login. Licences of the third-party data are unverified.
sources.novelty_threat_for_m08: This paper is direct prior art for most of what M08 could claim at G-STRUCT on C. elegans: (1) a compact stochastic developmental generator (cell types + birth times + soma distance + elongation-scaled decay + constant pruning) for the 180-neuron nerve ring; (2) cross-individual synapse prediction from worm 7 to worm 8 at AUROC ~0.78-0.81; (3) connectivity-inferred compact types (8 inferred types beat 13 Cook types; 4 match them); (4) the need for multiple developmental epochs and for pruning to follow the Witvliet stages; (5) reciprocity as the missing rule behind triad statistics; (6) heavy S+ compression (14 parameters); (7) model probability tracking cross-individual conservation (backbone) and synapse count. Any M08 rule on Witvliet data built from these features is REPLICATION_ONLY unless it beats this model and a memorization baseline on stricter held-out tests. The paper does not threaten G-FUNCTION or G-CONSTRUCT: it has no activity, function or construction component.
sources.gaps_m08_could_test: (1) Memorization baselines. Our quick check (Witvliet entry) shows that simply copying worm 7 already matches or beats the published model on AUROC for worm 8. Report accuracy against description length as a Pareto front and use AUPRC and held-out log-likelihood with bootstrap CIs, in both directions (7 to 8 and 8 to 7). (2) Count the full description length, including type labels, positions and birth times, not just S+. (3) Remove type-inference leakage: infer types only on training dyads, or only on a different worm, then re-run the split-half and backbone analyses. (4) Hold out a whole stage (train on all stages except k, predict k) with AUROC/AUPRC, compared against copying the nearest stage. (5) Ablations scored on held-out data: shuffle positions, shuffle birth times, drop elongation, set S- = 0, shuffle types. (6) Same-split comparison against a plain SBM on the same inferred types, a degree-corrected SBM, distance-only, Nicosia 2013-style economical growth, Varier & Kaiser 2011, the Barabási / Kovács genetic models using CeNGEN expression, and the Jonas & Kording IRM. (7) Transfer to an independent reconstruction (WormAtlas/White, Cook 2019 hermaphrodite) and to the male connectome. (8) Extend to gap junctions and synapse-count weights. (9) G-FUNCTION: test whether generated connectomes, under a fixed dynamics model, predict measured C. elegans activity or perturbation responses. The paper does not attempt this, and which datasets would serve is unverified.

sources.what_was_read: The whole JATS XML source (176,663 bytes), obtained via the bioRxiv API jatsxml link: all text, the full Methods, and the supplementary figure legends S1-S8. I did not see the figure images. The 12.5 MB lab-hosted PDF was not downloaded because it is over the 5 MB limit. I use this version as the best available stand-in for the unreachable PNAS SI Appendix. It may differ from the PNAS version.

key_findings.finding: Data preprocessing: 180 nerve-ring neurons from Witvliet, chemical synapses only, binarized, autapses removed. In this version 13 neurons were dropped for the multi-epoch analyses because of birth-time discrepancies. A later repository commit (35e8d6b3, 2024-07-30) is titled 'use the entire ensemble of 180 neurons ... models trained in developmental epochs', which suggests the PNAS version used all 180.

Fitting is a 40x40 grid over S- and beta0 (range given as [0, 0.05)), with S+ set by per-type binary search to match counts (tolerance 0.05) and the maximum-likelihood grid point selected. For the single-epoch model, dataset 8 is the test set and is not used in training.

Variability: the two Witvliet adults differ by a normalized Hamming distance of 0.04, while two model draws differ by 0.105 ± 0.002 (mean ± SD over 20 splits). So the model is more than twice as variable as the measured inter-individual difference. This number does not appear in the PNAS main text.

Same headline numbers as the PNAS version: AUROC 0.78 (13 types), 0.81 (8 inferred), 0.77 for the 9-parameter compressed model, JSD 0.01135 to 0.00045 bits, gamma = 7. The preprint has no Fig 7F/G synapse-count analysis, so no r = 0.35.

sources.model_or_method_spec: As in the PNAS entry. The preprint gives explicit formulas for the hit rate used in type clustering, the dynamic-programming quantization (minimum weighted sum of within-class variances; K+2 parameters), the exact Poisson-binomial degree and histogram moments, 4-state dyad recurrences for the reciprocal and multi-epoch models, and uniform birth-time noise in [-delta·w_i, delta·w_i).
sources.validation_design: Same as the PNAS entry.
stated_limitations: Each stage comes from a different individual, so the developmental path may not be realizable.
With only two adult worms, the model's variability cannot be compared properly with natural variability.

sources.citation: schneidmanlab/BrainBuildingPaper (GitHub repository; O. Richter, E. Schneidman). Created 2024-07-01, last push 2025-08-14 (commit d762ed07 'review updates'), 11 commits, 2 stars, 0 forks. Description uses the preprint title.
sources.what_was_read: From the GitHub API: repository metadata, the licence endpoint, the commit list and the full recursive tree (3,172 entries, not truncated). From raw.githubusercontent.com at d762ed07, all small text and code files: README, requirements.txt, cluster_cmds.txt, every .py file and every ClusterScripts/*.sh. Of paper_figures.py (199 KB) I searched function names and metric calls and read the Fig 1G, 2G, 3, 5, 6B/E and 7 functions. I unpickled no pickles. I also downloaded two small bundled data files (synapse_count_matrices.xlsx, 764,283 B, and NeuronPosition3D.csv, 6,825 B) into the scratchpad and parsed them with the standard library.

key_findings.finding: Licence: none. GitHub API license = null and GET /license returns 404, so no LICENSE file exists. By default the code is all-rights-reserved, so reuse or redistribution needs the authors' permission; that legal default is our inference.

Dependencies: Python 3.9, matplotlib 3.8.2, networkx 3.2.1, numpy 1.26.2, pandas 1.4.0, poisson-binomial 0.0.1 (the README says to patch its __init__.py line 54 by hand, fft -> fft.fft), scikit-learn 1.3.2, scipy 1.11.4, tqdm 4.66.1, mpmath 1.3.0. The code reads .xls and .xlsx through pandas, which needs xlrd/openpyxl; neither is listed (our observation).

A cluster is required. The README says the training parts 'require a computing cluster' (IBM LSF, WIS cluster). Each LSF job uses 1 core and 500 MB on the 'new-short' queue. Job arrays are multiples of 1600, one job per (S-, beta0) grid point: 20,800 jobs for type counts 1-13, 12,800 for the gamma scan 2-9, 32,000 for 20 splits, 24,000 for the overfitting control. SavedOutputs/ (trained parameters and likelihoods) and Figures/ are gitignored. No trained S+ matrices or likelihood tables are bundled, so the figures cannot be regenerated without re-running the grid.

Our rough estimate of CPU cost, not measured. The reference implementation is pure Python. For each type pair, each binary-search step reloads a pickle and loops over all ~32k ordered pairs, then runs a 10-min recurrence of up to 350 steps for that type's pairs. By our order-of-magnitude estimate that is tens of minutes per grid point, or hundreds of CPU-hours per 1600-point configuration, well beyond M08's 24 core-hour development budget. The recurrence is linear (p_n = c_n + (1 - S- - c_n)p_{n-1}), so a NumPy reimplementation vectorized over pairs should make a full grid feasible on a laptop CPU (not verified).

Mapping of figures to code. paper_figures.py: fig_1_* (Fig 1), fig_2_* (Fig 2), fig_graph_features_a-f (Fig 3), fig_inferred_types_bio_interpretation_* (Fig 4), fig_compressed_models_a_b/c/d (Fig 5), fig_6_a/b/d/e/f (Fig 6), worms_overlap, prob_hist_by_num_datasets, cum_prob_hist_by_num_datasets, mean_weighted_connectivity_matrix, prediction_vs_num_synapses_data (Fig 7), supplement_* (SI). Training: train_c_elegans_independent_model.py covers single epoch, Cook and inferred/random types, compression, noisy birth times and the synthetic control. train_c_elegans_reciprocal_model.py covers the gamma scan and the 1- vs 3-epoch dyad splits. Core math: c_elegans_independent_model_training.py and c_elegans_reciprocal_model_training.py. Simulator: ConnectomeDeveloper, CElegansNeuronsAdder, SynapsesAdder, SynapsesRemover. Type inference: er_block_model.greedy_type_aggregation. The call site is not in the repo, and the code does not record which adjacency matrix was passed in (the paper says worm 7).

Code-level details relevant to fairness (our reading). Fig 1G uses SubTypes Dataset7 to train and Dataset8 to test. Figs 3A-F compare against Dataset8. find_compact_representation_within_performance_tolerance selects the compression level by AUROC on Dataset8, the test worm. fig_compressed_models_c computes AUROC with the diagonal included, while other figures remove it. Fig 6B scores AUROC on the test half of Dataset8. find_max_likelihood_full_model calls df.sort_values without assigning the result, which is harmless only because each CSV holds one grid point (batch_size = 1).

Bundled data. The tree's blobs sum to 534.7 MB uncompressed; GitHub reports 123,991 KB packed. The largest single file is ~1.1 MB. Most of the bulk is pickles: 335.5 MB of dyad-split synapse lists (20 splits x train/test x 8 datasets) and 155 MB of birth-time-noised connectomes (10 levels x 100 repeats). Raw inputs: synapse_count_matrices.xlsx (764,283 B; Witvliet 8 datasets; 180 presynaptic columns x 224 postsynaptic rows), NeuronConnect.xls (534,016 B; WormAtlas), NeuronPosition3D.csv (6,825 B; 299 lines), time_of_birth.xls (22,528 B), CellTypes.xlsx (27,554 B), nerve_ring_neurons_subset.pkl, inferred type partitions for 1-179 types (InferredTypes/types/*.pkl), random partitions for 1-15 types, and processed networkx pickles for each type configuration.

read:richter.summary_for_m08:
Richter & Schneidman (PNAS 2025) is the closest prior work for M08's C. elegans structure line. I read the main text in full, plus the bioRxiv v1 Methods and SI legends (the PNAS SI itself was unreachable), the correction, and the GitHub code.

**The model.** Neurons appear at measured birth times (Pathak 2020) at fixed adult 3D positions (Skuhersky 2022). Every 10 minutes each absent ordered pair forms a synapse with probability S+[type_i, type_j]·exp(-beta_t·d). beta_t = beta0 times the measured body-length growth (16-fold over development). Every existing synapse is pruned with one constant probability S-. A reciprocity factor gamma = 7 is added when the reverse synapse already exists. S- and beta0 are fitted on a 40x40 maximum-likelihood grid. Each S+ is set by binary search so expected per-type-pair counts match the training worm.

The 'inferred' types come from greedy agglomerative clustering that maximises a block-model hit rate on the training worm's adjacency. In other words, they are a stochastic block model fitted to worm 7, not independent biology.

**What was tested.**
- **Across individuals:** a single pair, Witvliet adult worm 7 for training and adult worm 8 for testing (same lab, same stage). There is no reverse direction, no CI, no AUPRC and no calibration.
- **Across stages:** 20 random half-splits of neuron pairs, the same split at every stage. Training uses Witvliet datasets 2, 6 and 8 (one count constraint per epoch); testing uses the held-out halves at all stages. Stages are compared only by density trajectories and log-likelihood ratios. No whole stage or whole individual is held out.

**Reported results.**
- Cross-individual AUROC: 0.78 with 13 Cook types, 0.81 with 8 inferred types. 4 inferred types roughly match the 13 Cook types.
- Compression: accuracy saturates at 14 parameters; 9 parameters keep AUROC 0.77 (95%). The code picks the compression level by AUROC on the test worm.
- Reciprocity: observed reciprocity is about 4.5x the Erdős-Rényi value (≈0.0036). Adding gamma cuts the triad Jensen-Shannon divergence from 0.01135 to 0.00045 bits.
- Development: 3 epochs plus pruning are needed to follow Witvliet density across stages; one epoch reaches a similar adult ROC by a different path.
- Backbone: of worm 8's 1,933 connections, 1,279 are shared with worm 7 and 863 with all three adults, so at most about 45% is shared. Model probability correlates with mean synapse count (r = 0.35).
- Robustness: up to 50% birth-time noise barely changes accuracy.
- Variability (preprint only): two model draws differ by a normalized Hamming distance of 0.105, while the two real adults differ by 0.04.
- The correction (PNAS 2026, e2535197122) fixes only the colours in Figs 4A, 5B and 7F.

**What the paper does not test.** No neural activity, function, behaviour, perturbation, gap junctions, synapse weights (beyond the r = 0.35 correlation), other species, males, or comparison against published generators (Nicosia 2013 is cited but not run). Varier & Kaiser 2011 and Kovács, Barabási & Barabási 2020 are not cited; their ref 27 is Barabási & Barabási, Neuron 2020. G-FUNCTION and G-CONSTRUCT are untouched, so M08 is only pre-empted at G-STRUCT on Witvliet data. A reimplementation there is [REP] / REPLICATION_ONLY.

**My own check, not in the paper.** Simply copying worm 7 to predict worm 8, using the repo's bundled Witvliet xlsx, gives:

| Baseline | AUROC | AUPRC |
|---|---|---|
| Binary copy | 0.820 | 0.458 |
| Synapse-count copy | 0.824 | 0.596 |
| Count copy + reverse-count tie-break | 0.855 | 0.643 |
| Earliest-stage counts (dataset 1) to adult | 0.643 | not computed |
| Dataset 6 counts (27 h) to adult | 0.761 | not computed |

So the published compact model does not beat memorization on cross-individual AUROC. Its real claim is compactness. That claim excludes about 540 bits of type labels and all the position and birth-time inputs from the parameter count.

**Code.** github.com/schneidmanlab/BrainBuildingPaper has no licence (GitHub API license null, /license 404), so reuse rights are unclear. It is pure Python 3.9 and needs an IBM LSF cluster: job arrays of 1600 grid points, up to 32,000 jobs. Trained outputs (SavedOutputs/, Figures/) are not bundled. The repo holds 534.7 MB, mostly pickles, but everything needed to reimplement is under 1 MB of xlsx/csv/xls fetchable without login (Witvliet counts 764 KB, positions 6.8 KB, birth times 22.5 KB, Cook types 27.6 KB). My rough estimate is that the reference code needs hundreds of CPU-hours per configuration, while a NumPy reimplementation of the linear recurrence should be cheap on a laptop CPU (not measured).

**Recommended Gate 1/2 actions:**
- Reimplement the model, vectorized, as the Gate 3 positive control.
- Add copy-worm and nearest-stage-copy baselines plus a plain SBM and a degree-corrected SBM.
- Report AUPRC and held-out log-likelihood with bootstrap CIs, in both directions.
- Count full description length, including labels and inputs.
- Infer types on training dyads only.
- Add leave-one-stage-out tests and an independent-reconstruction test (WormAtlas / Cook 2019).

My scripts and data are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-null3351-Code-neural-primitive-research/67758993-59ff-487e-8108-e1cc3e5b2603/scratchpad/richter/scripts/ and /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-null3351-Code-neural-primitive-research/67758993-59ff-487e-8108-e1cc3e5b2603/scratchpad/richter/dl_data/. Nothing in the repository was modified.

datasets.name: Witvliet et al. 2021 developmental brain connectomes, connectivity tables (NemaNode API / WormWiring xlsx / Nature SI)
datasets.organism: C. elegans, wild-type Bristol N2 hermaphrodites (isogenic)
datasets.primary_citation: Witvliet D. et al. Connectomes across development reveal principles of brain maturation. Nature 596, 257-261 (2021). doi:10.1038/s41586-021-03778-8; PMC8756380 (author manuscript)
datasets.units_of_replication: 8 individuals, one EM volume each. NemaNode /api/datasets gives ages of ~0, 5, 8, 16, 23, 27, 50 and 50 h after birth. Only datasets 7 and 8 (two adults) are a same-age replicate pair. Stage labels disagree between sources: the paper text says 'three L1, two L2, and one L3' plus two adults, while the NemaNode/WormWiring file names label datasets 1-4 as L1, 5 as L2 and 6 as L3. Per the authors' methods, the stages are confounded with the pipeline: 3 EM-prep batches, TEM for datasets 2/6/7 vs SEM for 1/3/4/5/8, and an HPM100 freezer for 1-5 vs ICE for 6-8. The animals are biologically independent individuals, but they are not exchangeable replicates.
datasets.licence: I found no explicit data licence. The article carries only Springer's TDM licence per its Crossref licence field; Europe PMC isOpenAccess=N. The NemaNode repo (zhenlab-ltri/NemaNode) is GPL-3.0 per the GitHub API, but that covers the viewer software, not the data. The WormWiring pages I read have no licence text. Status: publicly downloadable without login, licence unspecified.
datasets.size: Verified sizes. NemaNode JSON: 8 files, 790,308 B in total (52,306-152,297 B each, measured from my download). WormWiring xlsx: 8 files, 290,978 B in total (sizes of the copies in the cect GitHub tree; HEAD requests confirmed file 1 at 21,805 B and file 8 at 53,143 B). Nature SI MOESM4: 837,124 B (HEAD request). According to a cect note, MOESM4 holds chemical synapses only and the WormWiring files add gap junctions. NemaNode cells table (/api/cells): 50,351 B.
datasets.format_and_version: NemaNode returns JSON edge lists [{pre, post, type: chemical|electrical, synapses}]. It is a live database API with no version tag. WormWiring xlsx files are dated 2022-09-28 by the Last-Modified header. NemaNode cells.json fields: name, class, type, neurotransmitter, embryonic, inhead, intail.
datasets.n_neurons_and_synapses: My counts from the NemaNode JSON (cells include muscles and other non-neuronal partners). Chemical edges/synapses: D1 775/1,296; D2 986/1,895; D3 1,012/2,128; D4 1,136/2,777; D5 1,515/4,116; D6 1,525/4,456; D7 2,202/7,467; D8 2,186/7,970. Gap-junction edges: 83-310. Cells per dataset: 187-222. Coverage is the brain only (nerve ring plus ventral ganglion; authors).
datasets.use_in_m08: Primary training/development data for G-STRUCT. Supports leave-one-stage-out prediction in temporal order, interpolation between stages, and the adult D7 vs D8 cross-individual test.
datasets.independent_validation_value: Moderate to low. There is one same-age replicate pair. Richter & Schneidman (PNAS 2025) already fit generative models on one Witvliet animal and predict others (I read their abstract and results text), so any cross-animal result on these data must be framed as a replication unless it uses new held-out conditions or new features.
datasets.risks: (1) Circular annotations. The neuron classes and L/R pairs come from White 1986 anatomy, which was partly defined by morphology and connectivity. The sensory/inter/motor/modulatory types come from prior literature. Witvliet's stable/variable/developmentally-dynamic edge labels are computed from these same 8 datasets, so they must never be inputs when predicting a held-out dataset. (2) Gap junctions are 'not thoroughly annotated' (NemaNode text) and the authors excluded them from their analyses. (3) The authors list as a limitation that there is only one connectome at most time points. (4) Stage is confounded with EM technique. (5) No data licence: keep a fetch script plus hashes in the repo and do not commit the raw files. (6) The NemaNode API is unversioned, so record the SHA-256 at fetch time; hashes are listed under recommended_minimal_subset.
datasets.verified_how: Read parts of the PMC8756380 full text via NCBI efetch: the abstract, the EM methods, the stable/variable sections, Data availability, Code availability and Limitations (not the whole paper). Queried the NemaNode API (/api/datasets, /api/cells, download-connectivity), fetched the JSON and counted edges myself. Read the WormWiring Witvliet page HTML. Sent HEAD requests for file sizes. Checked the licence fields in Crossref and Europe PMC. Read the cect validation note for MOESM4's content (a secondary source).
