datasets.format_and_version: xlsx adjacency matrices (chemical and gap junction, herm and male). The original, WormWiring and July 2020 corrected versions differ (cect notes ray-cell naming inconsistencies).
datasets.n_neurons_and_synapses: Authors: the hermaphrodite graph has 460 nodes (302 neurons, 132 muscles, 26 other end organs), 4,887 chemical and 1,447 gap-junction edges. The male graph has 579 nodes (385 neurons, 155 muscles, 39 end organs), 5,315 chemical and 1,755 gap-junction edges.
datasets.use_in_m08: Whole-animal reference and feature source for development only. Do not use it as an independent test individual against White N2U/JSH.
datasets.independent_validation_value: Low for cross-individual tests, because it shares EM series with White 1986. The male is a different sex, which a cross-sex test could use, but that is a different question.
datasets.risks: Composite animal. Cell-type re-assignments partly rest on connectivity: per the cect summary, RIM/RMF/RMG became interneurons and SAB/SIA/SIB became motor neurons, partly based on NMJ evidence. That makes the types circular for synapse prediction. Multiple file versions exist. No licence.
datasets.verified_how: Read parts of the PMC6889226 full text via NCBI efetch: the abstract, the adjacency-matrix methods and the WormWiring availability sentences. HEAD requests for sizes. Crossref licence field. cect validation and docs pages (secondary sources).

datasets.name: White et al. 1986 legacy datasets (N2U adult head, JSH L4 head, JSE adult tail, whole-animal compilation) as served by NemaNode / Durbin 1987 neurodata.txt
datasets.primary_citation: White J.G., Southgate E., Thomson J.N., Brenner S. Phil. Trans. R. Soc. Lond. B 314, 1-340 (1986). doi:10.1098/rstb.1986.0056
datasets.units_of_replication: N2U (adult) and JSH (L4) are two distinct animals. The 'whole' dataset is a composite; Skuhersky 2022 describes the original reconstruction as a mosaic of five worms (three adult hermaphrodites, one L4, one male).
datasets.url: https://nemanode.org/api/download-connectivity?datasetId=white_1986_n2u (also white_1986_jsh, white_1986_jse, white_1986_whole); Durbin neurodata.txt copy at github.com/openworm/ConnectomeToolbox/blob/main/cect/data/neurodata.txt
datasets.licence: Paper: Crossref shows only the Royal Society TDM policy. Digitised data (Durbin 1987 thesis, NemaNode): no licence found (unverified). NemaNode states that the individual muscle synapses were added by the Zhen lab in 2020.
datasets.size: NemaNode JSON: JSH 108,035 B; N2U 115,929 B; whole 179,950 B (measured from my download). cect neurodata.txt: 223,795 B (GitHub tree).
datasets.n_neurons_and_synapses: My counts from the NemaNode JSON (chemical edges/synapses; GJ edges): JSH 1,480/4,340, GJ 289; N2U 1,629/4,538, GJ 270; whole 2,386/7,943, GJ 575; cells 215/221/309.
datasets.use_in_m08: Out-of-lab held-out individuals (L4 and adult) for frozen rules trained on Witvliet. This is a domain-shift test: different era, annotators and sectioning.
datasets.independent_validation_value: Moderate. These are genuinely different animals from Witvliet's. However, they are the most-studied connectome, so a model 'sees' them through the literature, and Brittin 2021 and Cook 2019 are built on the same EM.
datasets.risks: Legacy annotation errors (Cook 2019 lists corrections such as the DVB/PVT swap). The muscles were re-annotated later. Annotation differences confound the cross-dataset comparison. Licence unverified. Model developers widely know these data, so the hold-out is not blind.
datasets.verified_how: NemaNode API data sources text, plus my download and edge counts. Crossref metadata. cect docs (secondary). I did not read the 1986 paper itself.

datasets.name: Varshney et al. 2011 whole-animal wiring compilation
datasets.primary_citation: Varshney L.R. et al. Structural properties of the Caenorhabditis elegans neuronal network. PLoS Comput Biol 7, e1001066 (2011). doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1001066; PMC3033362
datasets.units_of_replication: A compilation built from White et al. 1986, Durbin 1987 and new annotations of the original EMs. It is not an independent individual.
datasets.url: WormAtlas NeuronConnect.xls (https://www.wormatlas.org/neuronalwiring.html, could not be fetched); copy at github.com/openworm/ConnectomeToolbox/blob/main/cect/data/NeuronConnect.xls; NemaNode white_1986_whole
datasets.licence: Paper: CC BY 4.0 (Crossref; Europe PMC license 'cc by'). Data file on WormAtlas: unverified, because the page failed with a TLS certificate error.
datasets.size: cect copy of NeuronConnect.xls: 518,144 B; NeuronConnectFormatted.xlsx: 149,490 B (GitHub tree). WormAtlas original: unverified.
datasets.use_in_m08: Whole-animal reference graph (including the ventral cord) for baselines and features. Not a test individual.
datasets.independent_validation_value: None as an independent individual.
datasets.risks: Composite. It largely duplicates White 1986, and its overlap with the NemaNode 'whole' dataset is unknown in detail.
datasets.verified_how: Only secondary sources (cect Varshney_2011 docs page) plus Crossref and Europe PMC licence metadata. I fetched the full-text XML but did not read it.

datasets.name: Brittin et al. 2021 volumetric nerve-ring contactome (Zenodo 4383277)
datasets.organism: C. elegans hermaphrodite (L4 JSH and adult N2U EM series)
datasets.primary_citation: Brittin C.A. et al. A multi-scale brain map derived from whole-brain volumetric reconstructions. Nature 591, 105-110 (2021). doi:10.1038/s41586-021-03284-x; PMC11648602
datasets.units_of_replication: 2 animals (the same EM series as White's JSH and N2U), with left and right sides analysed as 4 'datasets'.
datasets.licence: Zenodo API: cc-by-4.0. The README also carries an MIT-style data permission notice ('Copyright 2020 C. Brittin, S. Emmons and N. Cohen'). The Nature article itself is not OA (Springer TDM). SI 3 licence: unspecified.
datasets.size: adjacency.tar.bz2 879,737 B; reference_graphs.tar.bz2 36,502 B; databases.tar.bz2 18,454,962 B (over 5 MB); population_spatial_models 3,836,352 B; brainmap 1,244,468 B. Whole record: 17,208,679,701 B, mostly TrakEM2 mipmaps. SI 3 (MOESM5) on Springer: 112,899 B (HEAD). The cect copy of the same-named file is 129,504 B, so the version difference is unverified.
datasets.use_in_m08: Membrane-contact null and baseline for the JSH and N2U animals (per-dataset adjacency), in parallel with the Witvliet contacts.
datasets.independent_validation_value: Not independent of White's synapses, since it is the same animals. It is a baseline only.
datasets.risks: The M-delta/C-delta/G-delta 'reference graphs' pool L/R homologs and L4+adult, so they are circular if the test is on JSH or N2U; use the per-dataset adjacency instead. The authors drop the smallest 35% of contacts (<0.4 um^2) as non-reproducible.
datasets.verified_how: Zenodo API (files, sizes, licence). Read the full README.txt. Read parts of the PMC11648602 full text via efetch: the abstract and the 'Conserved and variable circuits overlap' section. HEAD requests for the SI size.

datasets.name: Randi et al. 2023 neural signal propagation atlas (WT and unc-31): Nature Source Data, wormneuroatlas, OSF
datasets.primary_citation: Randi F., Sharma A.K., Dvali S., Leifer A.M. Neural signal propagation atlas of Caenorhabditis elegans. Nature 623, 406-414 (2023). doi:10.1038/s41586-023-06683-4; PMC10632145
datasets.units_of_replication: Authors: 113 WT-background animals and 18 unc-31 (dense-core-vesicle release defective) animals. 23,433 neuron pairs were measured (66% of possible head pairs), with 1 to 59 imaging repeats per pair. Neuron identity came from NeuroPAL. These are biologically independent of all the EM animals.
datasets.url: Source Data Fig. 2: https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41586-023-06683-4/MediaObjects/41586_2023_6683_MOESM5_ESM.xlsx ; Source Data Ext. Data Fig. 7 (unc-31): .../41586_2023_6683_MOESM15_ESM.xlsx ; Source Data Fig. 3: .../MOESM6_ESM.xlsx ; https://github.com/francescorandi/wormneuroatlas ; https://osf.io/e2syt/
datasets.licence: Article: CC BY 4.0 (Crossref VOR licence; Europe PMC 'cc by'). I assume the Source Data ESM is covered by the article licence but did not verify a separate credit line. wormneuroatlas: GPL-3.0 per the GitHub API and the PyPI classifier GPLv3+; this repo also contains funatlas.h5. OSF node e2syt: node_license null, so no licence is declared.
datasets.size: MOESM5: 996,970 B. MOESM15: 287,807 B. MOESM6: 1,006,070 B (all HEAD, and confirmed by download). funatlas.h5: 18,266,176 B (GitHub tree; not downloaded). PyPI wormneuroatlas 0.0.7.3 wheel: 37,760,635 B. OSF: exported_data.tar.gz 523,093,816 B; exported_data_unc31.tar.gz 84,924,311 B; exported_data_full.tar.gz 1,143,920,663 B; spont_data_fig6.zip 2,402,185 B.
datasets.format_and_version: MOESM5 sheets: 'Figure2a, df_over_f' and 'Figure2a, alpha=(1 - q_val)' (168×168, labelled by neuron name), plus Fig. 2c-g. MOESM15 sheets: 'EDFig7a, df f' and 'EDFig7a, qvalues' (unc-31; 164 rows × 109 stimulated columns), plus EDFig7b-c. MOESM6 sheets: Fig. 3b-d, anatomy-model ΔV vs measured.
datasets.n_neurons_and_synapses: My parse of MOESM5: 22,521 numeric WT ΔF/F cells out of 168×168 (untested pairs are blank); 979 cells with (1−q) > 0.95. My parse of MOESM15: 9,228 numeric unc-31 cells; 430 with q < 0.05. Authors: activity recorded from 186 of 188 head neurons.
datasets.use_in_m08: Independent G-FUNCTION and intervention validation. First freeze a generated or learned circuit and a fixed dynamics model (with parameters fitted only on training data or a declared split). Then predict which stimulated pairs propagate signal, and their sign and amplitude, in WT. Test whether the wired-only prediction fits unc-31 better than WT, as the authors found for anatomy.
datasets.independent_validation_value: High. These are independent animals and an independent modality (optogenetic stimulation plus calcium imaging), and they include a genetic perturbation. There is also a strong published baseline: the authors report that anatomy-derived predictions agree poorly with measured amplitudes (R^2 < 0 in Fig. 3d) even after fitting weights and signs.
datasets.risks: (1) The data measure multi-hop, effective propagation, not monosynaptic edges, so edge-level AUROC against these data is not valid. (2) Adult head only: no developmental stages. (3) Stimulation order was 'mostly randomly selected', and repeats per pair are uneven (1-59), so the q-values depend on sampling. (4) The authors' anatomy model used Witvliet adults 7/8 plus White, so our structure training data overlap with their baseline's inputs; that is fine for the baseline but must be declared. (5) unc-31 animals are less active, and the GUR-3/PRDX-2 system is drug-inducible, which adds a confound. (6) The OSF data carry no licence. (7) There is a risk of fitting dynamics on the WT test map: the read-out and dynamics must be frozen before opening the held-out pairs or unc-31.
datasets.verified_how: Read parts of the PMC10632145 full text (Europe PMC XML): the abstract, 'Functional measurements differ from anatomy', the anatomy-simulation methods, Data and Code availability, and animal counts. HEAD requests and downloads of MOESM5/6/15 (all under 1.1 MB), with sheets parsed via zipfile. GitHub API (repo licence and tree). PyPI JSON. OSF API (node metadata and file sizes). Read the wormneuroatlas README and the NeuroAtlas.py access functions (wt/unc31 dFF, q, q_eq, occ1).

datasets.name: Atanas et al. 2023 brain-wide activity and behaviour (WormWideWeb; Zenodo 8150515 and later versions)
datasets.organism: C. elegans adult hermaphrodites, freely moving
datasets.primary_citation: Atanas A.A., Kim J. et al. Brain-wide representations of behavior spanning multiple timescales and states in C. elegans. Cell 186, 4134-4151 (2023). doi:10.1016/j.cell.2023.07.035; PMC10836760
datasets.units_of_replication: Authors: 14 animals (16 min recordings, 143±12 head neurons each), 40 NeuroPAL/GCaMP7f animals, and 30 datasets with a noxious heat stimulus (19 of them NeuroPAL-labelled). Each animal is independent.
datasets.licence: Zenodo v1 (8150515) and 8185377: cc-by-3.0-us. The latest version, 19388374, has no licence field in the API (unverified). The code Zenodo record 8151918 says 'other-open', and the GitHub repo has no licence (API null). The paper is CC BY-NC 4.0 (Crossref VOR).
datasets.size: Latest version: processed_h5.tar.bz2 568,776,589 B; neuropal_label.json.bz2 16,169 B; record total ~32.99 GB. v1 total 32,312,069,478 B. Per-dataset WormWideWeb downloads are unverified: curl got a 'Page Not Found' page (7,162 B) on every path.
datasets.use_in_m08: Optional second functional check (spontaneous activity correlations; heat stimulus as a perturbation). Not in the minimal subset.
datasets.independent_validation_value: Medium. These are independent animals and behaviour, but the stimulus is a sensory perturbation, not a circuit intervention. A structure-to-function link would need a dynamics model plus a behaviour read-out.
datasets.risks: Over 5 MB. Nuclear GCaMP, so temporal and spatial resolution is limited (an authors' limitation). Their encoding model (CePNEM) is itself a fitted model. The authors' own connectome analyses used the averaged Witvliet adults. Licence varies by Zenodo version.
datasets.verified_how: Read parts of the PMC10836760 full text via efetch: the key resources table, data availability, heat-stimulus and NeuroPAL paragraphs, the connectome-used methods and the limitations heading. Zenodo API, including /versions. Read the GitHub README. Tried curl on wormwideweb.org.

datasets.name: Kato et al. 2015 and Uzel, Kato & Zimmer 2022 whole-brain imaging datasets
datasets.primary_citation: Kato S. et al. Cell 163, 656-669 (2015) doi:10.1016/j.cell.2015.09.034; Uzel K., Kato S., Zimmer M. Curr Biol (2022) doi:10.1016/j.cub.2022.06.039
datasets.units_of_replication: Unverified
datasets.url: Unverified. The Cell Press full text returned 403, neither paper is in PMC per Europe PMC, and web searches found no data deposit.
datasets.licence: Article licences (Crossref): Kato 2015 has the Elsevier open-access user licence (not CC); Uzel 2022 is CC BY 4.0. Data licence: unverified.
datasets.size: unverified
datasets.use_in_m08: Not planned. A possible later activity-dynamics benchmark if the data can be located.
datasets.independent_validation_value: Unknown until the data are located.
datasets.risks: Location, licence and identification quality are all unverified.
datasets.verified_how: Crossref and Europe PMC metadata only. Two web searches found no data repository. I did not read the full text.

datasets.name: CeNGEN single-cell neuronal gene expression (Taylor et al. 2021)
datasets.organism: C. elegans L4 hermaphrodite neurons (FACS plus 10x scRNA-seq); cengen.org also lists newer L1, adult hermaphrodite and male datasets
datasets.primary_citation: Taylor S.R. et al. Molecular topography of an entire nervous system. Cell 184, 4329-4347 (2021). doi:10.1016/j.cell.2021.06.023; PMC8710130
datasets.units_of_replication: Pooled animals. cengen.org says 100,955 sequenced cells from 17 experiments, assigned to 128 neuronal classes; the expression is class-level, not individual-level.
datasets.licence: I found no licence statement on the cengen.org downloads page. The article carries the Elsevier open-access user licence (Crossref), not CC. The CengenApp GitHub repo has no licence (API null). GEO terms: unverified.
datasets.size: Thresholded matrices: threshold1 14,921,760 B; threshold2 13,555,783 B; threshold3 11,612,055 B; threshold4 9,818,818 B. CeNGEN_aggr_bio_reps_101821.tsv 26,807,789 B; integrated TMM counts 28,508,298 B. All sizes from HEAD requests and all over 5 MB, so none were downloaded. The wormneuroatlas repo has copies (cengen.h5 32,852,608 B).
datasets.use_in_m08: Candidate generative feature (adhesion molecules, receptors and ligands per class) for G-STRUCT rules. Optional, and needs approval for an ~10-14 MB download.
datasets.independent_validation_value: As a feature it is independent of synapse measurement (different animals, a different modality). It is not a validation target.
datasets.risks: The class granularity is inherited from anatomy-defined classes, and L4 expression would be applied to L1-adult connectomes, a stage mismatch. Thresholds are a choice. Prior art: the authors already report that cell adhesion molecules correlate with neuron-specific connectivity. Licence unclear. Over 5 MB.
datasets.verified_how: Read parts of the PMC8710130 full text via efetch: the data availability and thresholding passages. Read the cengen.org home, downloads and single-cell pages. HEAD requests for sizes.

datasets.name: Ripoll-Sanchez et al. 2023 neuropeptidergic connectome (Figshare collection 6895870; NemaMod)
datasets.primary_citation: Ripoll-Sanchez L. et al. The neuropeptidergic connectome of C. elegans. Neuron 111, 3570-3589 (2023). doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2023.09.043; PMC7615469
datasets.units_of_replication: Model-derived networks (long-, mid- and short-range models) built from CeNGEN expression, peptide-GPCR deorphanization and anatomy. These are not measurements in individual animals.
datasets.licence: CC BY 4.0 on every Figshare article in the collection (Figshare API). Paper: CC BY 4.0 (Crossref). Code: MIT (LICENSE file).
datasets.size: Aggregate networks: short 185,773 B, mid 185,874 B, long 186,152 B. neuron_information.csv: 8,343 B. Ligand-receptor table: 1,265 B. 92 individual NPP-GPCR networks at ~185,444 B each. All from the Figshare API.
datasets.use_in_m08: An extrasynaptic explanatory feature for Randi pairs that are functionally connected without a wire, and a non-synaptic 'wireless' baseline.
datasets.independent_validation_value: Low as a validation target, because it is a model. It is moderate as an independent covariate for function.
datasets.risks: Circular for synapse prediction: per the authors, the mid- and short-range models constrain connections using anatomical regions and process bundles from the White and Witvliet anatomy. It inherits CeNGEN thresholds (threshold 4 chosen). Randi 2023 already reported peptidergic explanations, so this is prior art.
datasets.verified_how: Read parts of the PMC7615469 full text (Europe PMC XML): the model definitions, data availability and threshold choice. Figshare API (collection, articles, licences, file sizes). Raw LICENSE from GitHub.

datasets.name: Neuron birth times transcribed from Sulston lineages (Pathak, Chatterjee & Sinha 2020, S5 Table); Sulston 1977/1983
datasets.primary_citation: Pathak A., Chatterjee N., Sinha S. PLoS Comput Biol 16, e1007602 (2020) doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1007602 (PMC6959611); Sulston & Horvitz 1977 doi:10.1016/0012-1606(77)90158-0; Sulston et al. 1983 doi:10.1016/0012-1606(83)90201-4
datasets.units_of_replication: A canonical, invariant lineage, so there are no per-individual values. Per the table caption, S5 was 'manually transcribed from lineage charts' in Sulston 1977/1983.
datasets.licence: S5 Table: CC BY 4.0 as part of the PLOS article (Crossref; Europe PMC 'cc by'). The code repo has no licence (GitHub API null). The Sulston papers carry an Elsevier TDM licence only.
datasets.size: S5 Table .xls: 22,528 B. S4 Table: 36,352 B (HEAD after redirect). Repo files are small (e.g. ar_bt.mat 12,590 B). wormneuroatlas cell_lineage.txt: 83,696 B (an alternative source in a GPL-3 repo).
datasets.use_in_m08: Generative feature (birth-time cohort, lineage distance) for developmental rules.
datasets.independent_validation_value: As a feature it is independent of the connectome (lineage was observed in living animals). It is not a validation target.
datasets.risks: Manual transcription errors. Richter & Schneidman 2025 already use exactly this table (their ref. 40) together with Witvliet, so a model using it is a replication unless it adds something new. Witvliet staged their larvae partly against the lineage, which is a mild coupling.
datasets.verified_how: Read parts of the PMC6959611 full text (Europe PMC XML): the abstract, Data Availability and the supplementary file list with captions. HEAD requests for sizes. GitHub contents API. I did not open the .xls.

datasets.name: Skuhersky et al. 2022 3D neuron position atlas (NeuroPAL-derived); NeuroPAL data (Yemini et al. 2021)
datasets.primary_citation: Skuhersky M. et al. Toward a more accurate 3D atlas of C. elegans neurons. BMC Bioinformatics 23, 195 (2022) doi:10.1186/s12859-022-04738-3 (PMC9145532); Yemini E. et al. NeuroPAL. Cell 184, 272-288 (2021) doi:10.1016/j.cell.2020.12.012
datasets.units_of_replication: The authors say at least 7 animals per neuron, aggregated into an atlas. The CSV holds only mean coordinates: on inspection it has 300 rows with 4 columns (name, x, y, z).
datasets.licence: Paper: CC BY 4.0 (Crossref). The elegans-atlas repo has no licence (GitHub API null). NeuroPAL Zenodo: mit-license (Zenodo API).
datasets.size: LowResAtlas.csv: 6,799 B. LowResAtlasWithHighResHeadsAndTails.csv: 6,762 B. NeuroPAL data.zip: 1,118,208,396 B (not downloaded).
datasets.use_in_m08: Soma-position and distance feature for spatial wiring rules.
datasets.independent_validation_value: As a feature it is independent of the EM connectomes (fluorescence imaging, different animals).
datasets.risks: Adult positions would be applied to L1-L3 connectomes, a stage mismatch. There is no per-neuron variance in the CSV. There is no repo licence. Richter & Schneidman 2025 use it (their ref. 41), so this is replication territory.
datasets.verified_how: Read parts of the PMC9145532 full text (Europe PMC XML): the abstract, conclusions and data availability. GitHub API tree. Read the CSV head and line count over raw.githubusercontent.com. Zenodo API for NeuroPAL. NeuroPAL data availability sentence from PMC10494711 via efetch.

datasets.name: Yim et al. 2024 dauer connectome and contactome
datasets.primary_citation: Yim H. et al. Comparative connectomics of dauer reveals developmental plasticity. Nat Commun 15, 1546 (2024). doi:10.1038/s41467-024-45943-3; PMC10899629
datasets.units_of_replication: 1 dauer animal (the authors list this as a limitation).
datasets.url: https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41467-024-45943-3/MediaObjects/41467_2024_45943_MOESM6_ESM.xlsx (Supplementary Data 3, synaptic) ; ..._MOESM9_ESM.xlsx (Supplementary Data 6, contact) ; EM at bossdb.org/project/yim_choe_bae2023
datasets.licence: Article: CC BY 4.0 (Crossref; Europe PMC). Code (jabae/Yim-Choe-Bae-et_al-2024): GPL-3.0 (LICENSE file).
datasets.size: Supplementary Data 3 (MOESM6): 3,369,709 B. Supplementary Data 6 (MOESM9): 3,860,635 B (HEAD). Copies of the same size are in cect/data.
datasets.n_neurons_and_synapses: Authors: 181 neuron nodes and 1,995 neuronal connections (2,200 including NMJs). No gap junctions.
datasets.use_in_m08: Optional out-of-distribution stage test: does a frozen developmental rule extrapolate to an alternative developmental stage? It also provides a contact baseline.
datasets.independent_validation_value: Medium. It is a new individual at a new stage, but there is only one animal, and the pipeline differs.
datasets.risks: Synapses were detected automatically by a CNN and weighted by active-zone volume, unlike the manual counts in Witvliet, so a method shift confounds any stage effect. No gap junctions. Single animal.
datasets.verified_how: Read parts of the PMC10899629 full text (Europe PMC XML): the abstract, data and code availability, and the passages on Supplementary Data 3/6 and the single-dauer limitation. HEAD requests for sizes. Crossref licence.

datasets.name: OpenWorm ConnectomeToolbox (cect) and c302
datasets.primary_citation: github.com/openworm/ConnectomeToolbox; github.com/openworm/c302
datasets.units_of_replication: Re-packages the sources above (Witvliet 1-8, White, Varshney, Cook, Brittin, Yim, Ripoll-Sanchez, Bentley, Randi/WormNeuroAtlas and others). It adds no new animals.
datasets.licence: MIT for the code (GitHub API; PyPI classifiers for cect 0.3.5 and c302 0.12.1; LICENSE 'Copyright (c) 2026 OpenWorm'). The cect docs have no data-licence statement, so redistributed data keep their original licences (or lack of one). MIT does not relicense them.
datasets.size: cect 0.3.5 wheel: 13,634,816 B; c302 0.12.1 wheel: 3,803,638 B (PyPI); both over or near the limit, not installed. Individual data files are small, e.g. witvliet_2020_*.xlsx at 21,805-53,165 B and the cache WormNeuroAtlasFuncReader.json at 451,368 B. Repo size per the GitHub API: 722,431 KB.
datasets.use_in_m08: Cross-check for parsing and readers (validation pages list expected edge weights), and a convenient mirror of small SI files with provenance notes. Not a primary source.
datasets.independent_validation_value: None. It is a mirror.
datasets.risks: Derived caches lose information: the Randi cache keeps only pairs with q<0.05, so 'untested' and 'tested, not connected' become indistinguishable. Some mirrored files differ in size from the publisher copies (Brittin SI 3: 129,504 vs 112,899 B). Using its readers adds its own neuron-name normalisations.
datasets.verified_how: GitHub API repo metadata and recursive tree. Raw README, LICENSE, docs pages (Witvliet_2021, Brittin_2021, Cook_2019, Randi_2023, RipollSanchez_2023, Varshney_2011, White_1986, Atanas_2023, Yim_2024, Taylor_2021, Resources) and validation pages. PyPI JSON.

datasets.name: Richter & Schneidman 2025 BrainBuildingPaper repo (prior-art model and processed data)
datasets.primary_citation: Richter O., Schneidman E. Building the connectome of a small brain with a simple stochastic developmental generative model. PNAS (2025) doi:10.1073/pnas.2504913122; PMC12664000
datasets.units_of_replication: Uses the Witvliet individuals (the authors fit one animal and predict held-out parts or another individual), Cook 2019 types, Pathak birth times and Skuhersky positions (per their references 15, 16, 40, 41).
datasets.licence: Paper: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (Crossref VOR). Repo: no licence (GitHub API license null).
datasets.size: Repo size per the GitHub API: 123,991 KB. The file list was not verified because the GitHub API rate limit was hit; the README says the CElegansData folder holds raw and processed data.
datasets.use_in_m08: A mandatory published-model baseline to reproduce, since the brief's §4.1 names it as the direct precedent. It also defines which held-out conditions would count as new.
datasets.independent_validation_value: None. It is prior art.
datasets.risks: Their 'inferred cell types' come from clustering the connectome itself, so they are circular unless re-inferred on training animals only. With no licence, code reuse needs care: re-implement from the paper, or cite and run without redistributing.
datasets.verified_how: Read parts of the PMC12664000 full text (Europe PMC XML): the abstract and significance statement, the Data/Software availability statement, the reference list and a few results sentences. GitHub API repo metadata (licence null). Read the raw README.

read:celegans_data.recommended_minimal_subset:
This subset is legal and needs no login: about 4.25 MB core, or about 6.1 MB with two optional baseline and cross-check files. Every file is under 5 MB. Store a fetch script and SHA-256 hashes in the repo, not the raw files, because several sources have no declared licence.

(a) Cross-individual and cross-stage structure prediction (2,964,616 B):
1. Witvliet connectivity, 8 datasets, from the NemaNode API download-connectivity?datasetId=witvliet_2020_1..8: 790,308 B in total. Includes chemical and electrical edges, plus ages of 0/5/8/16/23/27/50/50 h from /api/datasets.
2. NemaNode /api/cells: 50,351 B. Gives class, type, neurotransmitter and the embryonic flag. Treat the class and type labels as anatomy-derived priors and record them in the knowledge budget.
3. Same-individual membrane-contact baseline from dwitvliet/nature2021, data/physical_contact (Dataset1-6 and 8, adjacency plus volumes): 990,929 B. Licence: none declared.
4. Out-of-lab held-out animals White 1986 JSH (L4) and N2U (adult) from NemaNode: 108,035 + 115,929 = 223,964 B.
5. Brittin 2021 adjacency.tar.bz2 from Zenodo 4383277: 879,737 B, CC BY 4.0. Contact baseline for JSH and N2U. Do not use the pooled M4 reference graphs as truth.
6. Birth times, Pathak 2020 S5 Table: 22,528 B, CC BY 4.0.
7. Soma positions, Skuhersky LowResAtlas.csv: 6,799 B. The repo has no licence; the paper is CC BY.

Cross-check: Witvliet Nature SI MOESM4 (837,124 B, chemical-only matrices) or the 8 WormWiring xlsx files (290,978 B, which include gap junctions).

Suggested splits:
- Develop on Witvliet D1-D6 plus D7.
- Hold out D8 as the cross-individual test against the D7 adult.
- Use JSH and N2U as the out-of-lab test.
- Use leave-one-stage-out over D1-D6 for cross-stage tests.
- Optional out-of-distribution stage: Yim 2024 dauer, Supplementary Data 3 + 6 (3,369,709 + 3,860,635 B, CC BY 4.0). This adds 7.23 MB and is confounded by the different synapse-detection pipeline.

(b) One independent functional and perturbation validation (1,284,777 B, CC BY 4.0 per the article):
8. Randi 2023 Source Data Fig. 2, 41586_2023_6683_MOESM5_ESM.xlsx (996,970 B): WT 168×168 ⟨ΔF/F⟩ and (1−q) matrices.
9. Randi 2023 Source Data Extended Data Fig. 7, 41586_2023_6683_MOESM15_ESM.xlsx (287,807 B): unc-31 ΔF/F and q matrices, 164×109.

Optional baseline file: MOESM6_ESM.xlsx (1,006,070 B), the authors' anatomy-model ΔV vs measured values.

Test design: freeze the structure rule and the dynamics model, predict WT propagation at the pair level, then test whether the wired-only prediction tracks unc-31 better than WT. Do not score the predictions as monosynaptic edges.

Working copies are in scratch, outside the repo, at /tmp/claude-501/m08dl/nemanode/*.json and /tmp/claude-501/m08dl/randi/MOESM{5,6,15}.xlsx. SHA-256 hashes:
- w1 d084b110…, w8 5aa27719…, white_1986_n2u 76777087…, white_1986_jsh 654da321…, cells 377450f6…
- MOESM5 f02c68c9…, MOESM15 534e6ddf…, MOESM6 50679b56…
- The NemaNode API is unversioned, so re-hash at every fetch.

Files that would need explicit approval because they are over 5 MB: wormneuroatlas funatlas.h5 (18,266,176 B, for kernels, occurrence counts and q_eq), CeNGEN threshold matrices (9.8-14.9 MB), Witvliet per-individual skeletons (7.1-27.3 MB each) and Witvliet synapse-level JSON (7,332,352 B in total).
blocked_items: Zenodo 5637219 (Witvliet) holds only 3D meshes and a Blender file (902,400,553 B + 225,208,616 B, CC BY 4.0), not connectivity tables. The connectivity actually lives at NemaNode, WormWiring, Nature SI MOESM4 and github.com/dwitvliet/nature2021.

No explicit data licence was found for: the Witvliet connectivity (NemaNode, WormWiring, Nature SI; the article has only Springer's TDM licence and is not OA), the dwitvliet/nature2021 contact data (GitHub licence null), the Cook 2019 SI 5 / WormWiring files (fair-use statement only), the White/Durbin digitised data, OSF e2syt (node_license null), the Skuhersky elegans-atlas repo, the BrainBuildingPaper repo, the CeNGEN downloads, and the latest Atanas Zenodo version 19388374 (licence field absent). All are accessible without login, but redistribution rights are unverified.
The Witvliet Nature article page redirected to an idp.nature.com authorization flow, which I did not follow. I used the PMC author manuscript PMC8756380 instead.
WormAtlas (neuronalwiring.html, Varshney NeuronConnect.xls) failed with a TLS certificate error. The file's licence is unverified; a copy is in cect (518,144 B).

WormWideWeb returned a 'Page Not Found' page (7,162 B) on every path via curl, so the per-dataset downloads and their licence are unverified. The Atanas processed_h5.tar.bz2 is 568,776,589 B, over the limit.
Kato 2015 and Uzel 2022: the data repository location and licence are unverified. Cell Press returned 403, neither paper is in PMC, and web searches turned up no deposit.

Over the 5 MB rule, so not downloaded: wormneuroatlas funatlas.h5 18,266,176 B; wormneuroatlas wheel 37.8 MB; OSF e2syt exports 84.9 MB to 1.14 GB; CeNGEN matrices 9.8-28.5 MB; Brittin databases 18.5 MB and mipmaps (record total 17.2 GB); Witvliet skeletons 109.9 MB in total; NeuroPAL data.zip 1.12 GB; Atanas Zenodo ~33 GB; BossDB EM volumes; cect wheel 13.6 MB.
The GitHub API rate limit was hit before I could list the schneidmanlab/BrainBuildingPaper tree and the licences of lrvarshney/elegans. Those details are unverified.

Witvliet staging is inconsistent between sources: the paper says three L1, two L2 and one L3; the file names label 1-4 as L1, 5 as L2 and 6 as L3; the Zenodo README mentions an 'L5'. Use hours after birth from NemaNode rather than stage names.
I did not read the Sulston 1977/1983 originals or the White 1986 paper; birth times rely on Pathak's transcription. I read Varshney 2011 only through secondary sources (cect summary) and metadata.
read:celegans_data.summary_for_m08:
Gate 1's hard exit condition can be met legally without login, using about 4.25 MB of files that are each under 5 MB.

Structure data:
- The 8 Witvliet developmental connectomes from NemaNode (0.79 MB). These are 8 isogenic individuals aged ~0-50 h; datasets 7 and 8 are the only same-age adult pair.
- Same-individual membrane-contact baselines from dwitvliet/nature2021 (0.99 MB, 7 of 8 datasets).
- Two out-of-lab held-out animals, White JSH (L4) and N2U (adult), from NemaNode (0.22 MB).
- The Brittin contactome adjacency for those two animals (0.88 MB, CC BY 4.0).
- Features that are independent of the connectomes: Sulston-derived birth times (Pathak S5, 22.5 KB, CC BY) and NeuroPAL-derived soma positions (Skuhersky CSV, 6.8 KB).

Functional and perturbation data, independent of the EM animals:
- Randi 2023 Source Data, CC BY 4.0: the WT 168×168 signal-propagation ΔF/F and q matrices (MOESM5, 0.997 MB; 113 animals per the authors) and the unc-31 matrices (MOESM15, 0.288 MB; 18 animals).
- These give G-FUNCTION a real intervention test. The published anatomy baseline is already poor (the authors report R^2 < 0 for amplitudes), so 'beating anatomy' is a low bar. Pre-register a stronger comparison: our frozen rule against the actual connectome under the same frozen dynamics, and the WT vs unc-31 asymmetry.

Six issues Gate 2 must plan around:
1. Licences. The core structural data (Witvliet connectivity, NemaNode, WormWiring, nature2021 contacts, White/Cook digitisations) have no declared open licence. Keep fetch scripts and hashes, not copies, in the repo. Only Brittin's Zenodo record, the Randi and Yim articles, Ripoll-Sanchez's Figshare collection and Pathak's tables are explicitly CC BY.
2. Prior-art overlap. Richter & Schneidman (PNAS 2025) already use Witvliet individuals plus Pathak birth times, Skuhersky positions and Cook types for cross-animal and developmental generation. Any cross-individual result on Witvliet alone is a replication. Novelty has to come from new held-out conditions (White JSH/N2U, the Yim dauer, Randi function and unc-31) or from genuinely new rule classes, and their model must be reproduced as a baseline.
3. Circularity. Neuron classes and L/R pairs come from the anatomy, Cook's types partly from connectivity, and Witvliet's stable/variable/dynamic labels and Brittin's pooled M-delta graphs from the very datasets we would predict. Exclude these from inputs, or recompute them on training animals only. Ripoll-Sanchez's peptide networks embed anatomical bundle constraints. Same-individual contact maps leak the test animal's geometry and must be reported as a separate condition.
4. Confounds. In Witvliet, stage is confounded with EM technique (TEM vs SEM, freezer, 3 prep batches). There is only one replicate pair, and the dauer uses a different automated pipeline.
5. Scope of the Randi data. They measure multi-hop propagation in adult heads only, so no developmental functional test exists in this subset.
6. Paused for approval or unverified. CeNGEN expression (≥9.8 MB, licence unclear) and funatlas.h5 (18.3 MB) are over the size limit. Atanas, Kato and Uzel activity data were unverified or too large and are not needed for the minimal path.

Reading depth: I read the full text only in part (abstract, data availability, key methods and limitations) for Witvliet, Cook, Brittin, Randi, Atanas, Taylor, Ripoll-Sanchez, Skuhersky, Pathak, Yim and Richter–Schneidman. Varshney and White were secondary sources only, and Kato and Uzel metadata only. All sizes and licences above come from the Zenodo, GitHub, Figshare, OSF, PyPI, Crossref and Europe PMC APIs, or from HEAD requests and downloads I made myself. Edge counts and matrix counts are my own parses, not author figures.

datasets.name: flyvis motion-pathway connectome + literature tuning benchmarks (Lappalainen et al. 2024)
datasets.organism: Drosophila melanogaster (adult optic lobe, right-eye central field)
datasets.primary_citation: Lappalainen JK et al. Connectome-constrained networks predict neural activity across the fly visual system. Nature 634:1132-1140 (2024), doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07939-3, PMC11525180
datasets.format_and_version: flyvis/connectome/fib25-fib19_v2.2.json (JSON: nodes, edges with hex-lattice offsets, sign 'alpha', references). Package flyvis 1.2.0 on PyPI (wheel 385,602 B bundles the JSON); GitHub TuragaLab/flyvis main, last push 2026-10-14
datasets.n_neurons_and_synapses: I checked the JSON: 65 node types (the paper says 64, because CT1 is counted twice), 605 type-to-type chemical edges (paper: 604), signs 377 excitatory and 228 inhibitory, 2,140 offset entries, about 8,087 summed average synapses per postsynaptic cell. The paper reports the tiled model as 45,669 neurons and 1,513,231 synapses over 721 columns. Source: FIB-25 (7 medulla columns, 702 neurons) plus FIB-19 (1,099 neurons), per the paper.
datasets.units_of_replication: One consensus connectome, compiled from 2 EM volumes of different flies and averaged into spatially invariant filters. It does not give independent replicates per individual. The benchmarks are about 26 literature studies summarised as categorical labels: ON/OFF polarity for 32 types, direction-selectivity labels, and 12-direction T4/T5 tuning curves digitised from Maisak et al. 2013. These are not raw recordings.
datasets.licence: Code and bundled connectome: MIT. Checked via the GitHub API license field and the LICENSE text ('Copyright (c) 2023 Janne K. Lappalainen, ...'). Article: CC BY 4.0 (PMC page). SI zip: no separate licence found (unverified). Sintel training data: licence unverified.
datasets.size: Verified: JSON 618,148 B (sha256 bfbb0766...223351a); groundtruth_utils.py 10,004 B; responses_norm.h5 57,480 B; repo about 193 MB (GitHub API size, mostly docs images); PyPI wheel 385,602 B and sdist 30,073,117 B. Lappalainen Supplementary Data zip is 26,522,689 B by HEAD request. Per the PMC description it holds 7 files: type-to-type filters, connectome source refs, type matrix, a single-neuron connectome for 91 columns, refs and BibTeX for the 26 activity studies, and a catalogue of predicted responses for all 64 types. MPI-Sintel-complete.zip is 5,627,783,629 B by HEAD request. The pretrained-model zips download from Google Drive; their sizes are unverified.
datasets.use_in_m08: Development and structure source for the recommended T4 circuit. It supplies the input set and signs for T4/T5 (verified for T4a: Mi1+, Tm3+, Mi4-, Mi9-, C3-, CT1(M10)-, plus small C2, Mi10, TmY15, T4 and T5 inputs) and the spatial offsets. The literature labels are for development or sanity checks only. The DMN ensemble predictions in the SI catalogue are a prior-art baseline, not a target.
datasets.independent_validation_value: Moderate on its own. Without fitting to them, a structure-generated model can be scored against ON/OFF polarity for 32 types, T4/T5 direction selectivity and preferred direction, and the Maisak 2013 T4/T5 tuning curves. The paper reports that no neural recordings were used in training. These targets are still coarse, public and categorical. Value is much higher when paired with Groschner 2022 raw recordings.
datasets.risks: (1) Circularity of signs: most signs cite 'NernPC2018' (286 of 605 edges reference it). These come from transmitter/receptor profiling, not physiology, but polarity follows largely from sign propagation. The authors themselves report that accurate contrast prediction required sign measurements, so a sign-product-along-path baseline is mandatory (my inference). (2) The benchmark labels are well known to the designers, which is H0-PRIOR leakage, so they cannot serve as confirmation. (3) The connectome is spatially averaged and periodic, with no individual variability. (4) Edge count is 605 in the JSON and 604 in the paper; unresolved. (5) Using the pretrained models requires running a CLI script that calls the Google Drive API with an API key embedded in the package (flyvis_cli/download_pretrained_models.py). I did not use it, and it should be avoided or decided by the user. (6) Retraining as in the paper needs Sintel (5.6 GB, licence unverified) and GPU.
datasets.verified_how: GitHub API (license=MIT, size), git-tree API listing with file sizes, and the raw LICENSE, readme, groundtruth_utils.py, download_pretrained_models.py and docs connectome tutorial. I downloaded the 618 KB JSON to the scratchpad and parsed counts. PyPI JSON API for package sizes; wheel downloaded and listed. Paper: I read the PMC full text through an automated WebFetch extractor in two passes covering the whole page (methods, results, limitations, data statement); the PMC supplementary descriptions were read from the HTML. Springer ESM sizes and Sintel size came from HEAD requests. I did not open the SI zip because it exceeds 5 MB.

datasets.name: Groschner et al. 2022 T4 ON-motion circuit recordings and perturbations (Edmond doi:10.17617/3.8G)
datasets.primary_citation: Groschner LN, Malis JG, Zuidinga B, Borst A. A biophysical account of multiplication by a single neuron. Nature 603 (2022), doi:10.1038/s41586-022-04428-3, PMC8891015
datasets.format_and_version: Dataverse dataset version 1 (released 2021-12-14): 74 files of .npy, .csv, .tif, .ipynb and .swc, plus environment.yml
datasets.n_neurons_and_synapses: Whole-cell patch-clamp recordings. Array shapes read from npy headers: fig3_T4v (33, 2 polarities, 2 directions PD/ND, 8000 samples at 1 kHz). Input cells as (2 stimuli, n, 8000): Mi1 n=24, Tm3 n=12, Mi4 n=19, Mi9 n=29, C3 n=16. fig4 T4 Vm: GFP control (33, 2, 2, 3000) and GluCl-alpha RNAi (15, 2, 2, 3000). fig1e T4 spatiotemporal receptive fields: (17, 17, 210, 46 cells). The paper reports T4 amplitude n=53 wild type vs n=30 RNAi. No connectome synapses are included, only one EM T4 morphology (.swc).
datasets.units_of_replication: Individual cells, each from a different animal per the paper's methods (as extracted). Input-cell and T4 recordings come from different flies, not simultaneous recordings. Stimuli: ON/OFF edges at 30 deg/s (fig3/fig4), white-noise RF mapping, gratings in 8 directions, and 36-direction edges. Perturbations: GluCl-alpha RNAi and Nmdar1 RNAi in T4, plus pneumatic transmitter application. Behaviour: open loop n of about 18-20 flies, closed-loop bar fixation 16 flies per genotype (paper).
datasets.url: https://doi.org/10.17617/3.8G (API: https://edmond.mpg.de/api/datasets/:persistentId/?persistentId=doi:10.17617/3.8g ; files: https://edmond.mpg.de/api/access/datafile/<id>, e.g. 104815 fig3_T4v.npy, 104820 fig4_T4_vm_gfp.npy, 104821 fig4_T4_vm_gluclarnai.npy, 104811 Mi1, 104816 Tm3, 104812 Mi4, 104813 Mi9, 104809 C3, 104769 fig1e RFs)
datasets.licence: CC BY 4.0. Source: the Dataverse API license field as returned through WebFetch. The Zenodo stub record 8318693 is also cc-by-4.0 (Zenodo API).
datasets.size: Total 5,913,513,920 B across 74 files (API). The recommended subset is about 26.3 MB (sizes per API): fig3_Mi1 3,072,128; fig3_Tm3 1,536,128; fig3_Mi4 2,432,128; fig3_Mi9 3,712,128; fig3_C3 2,048,128; fig3_T4v 8,448,128; fig4_T4_vm_gfp 3,168,128; fig4_T4_vm_gluclarnai 1,440,128; fig3.ipynb 263,853; fig4.ipynb 150,817; readme.txt 824. Optional: fig1e_receptive_fields.npy 22,334,048. Large files to avoid: fig1fg_grating.csv 581,914,740 and fig5_R39H12_edges.csv 2,615,183,478.
datasets.use_in_m08: Independent functional validation for the T4 circuit (G-FUNCTION). The T4 traces, T4 RFs and RNAi T4 traces are held out. Input-cell traces may serve as measured drive. No parameter may be fitted on T4 data before freezing.
datasets.independent_validation_value: High. A structure-generated circuit can be scored without fitting on: (a) the T4 PD vs ND response and DSI to ON edges, and ON vs OFF selectivity; (b) T4 Vm time-course correlation; (c) the direction and size of the GluCl-alpha RNAi effect, where the paper reports amplitude falling from 18.10 to 13.63 mV and broader tuning, against the model with glutamatergic Mi9-to-T4 inhibition removed; (d) T4 spatial receptive-field structure (46 cells) against connectome-derived input offsets. flyvis was trained without these recordings. Whether Groschner 2022 is among Lappalainen's 26 benchmark studies is unverified.
datasets.risks: (1) Prior art: Groschner already fitted a conductance model (gain and threshold per input, E_leak, g_leak, SBI) to these data, and the T4 mechanism (Mi1/Tm3 excitation, Mi9 and Mi4/C3 offset inhibition) is known. Any 'discovered' rule matching it is a reproduction (H0-KNOWN). (2) The Mi9 inhibitory sign and the GluCl-alpha interpretation are already encoded in the connectome sign labels, so the RNAi prediction is partly built in. (3) The fig3 analysis notebook shifts input traces 'assuming an inter-ommatidial angle of 4.8 deg', which is a modelling assumption, not a measurement. (4) Edge stimuli use a single speed, so held-out stimulus diversity is limited, and inputs and T4 come from different animals. (5) fig1d_receptive_fields.npy is a pickled Python object (np.load with allow_pickle=True). Loading it can execute code, so treat it as untrusted and avoid it or open it only in isolation. (6) Female flies only, with no blinding (paper). (7) The cells-vs-repeats meaning of the first axis is my inference from the notebooks.
datasets.verified_how: Dataverse API metadata read through WebFetch: title, CC BY 4.0, 74 file names, sizes, ids, md5. With curl I fetched only the first 256 bytes of 13 .npy files (HTTP range) to read dtype and shape headers. I downloaded fig1.ipynb and fig4.ipynb (each under 5 MB) and read their load code; fig3.ipynb and readme were read via WebFetch. Paper: the PMC full text was processed by WebFetch over the first 100k of 121k characters (methods, results, limitations, data statement). The final part was not read.

datasets.name: Shiu et al. 2024 whole-brain LIF model: feeding (sugar/water/bitter) and antennal grooming circuits (philshiu/Drosophila_brain_model)
datasets.organism: Drosophila melanogaster (adult female brain, FlyWire FAFB)
datasets.primary_citation: Shiu PK et al. A Drosophila computational brain model reveals sensorimotor processing. Nature 634:210-219 (2024), doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07763-9, PMC11446845
datasets.format_and_version: Parquet connectivity and CSV completeness lists for FlyWire v630 (used in the paper) and v783 (public). Brian2 model.py. Supplementary Tables 1-12 as xlsx.
datasets.n_neurons_and_synapses: The paper models 127,400 proofread neurons (v630). Each neuron is excitatory or inhibitory by majority predicted transmitter, with weights from synapse counts and one free scale W_syn = 0.275 mV. I did not count edges in the parquet (not downloaded).
datasets.units_of_replication: One connectome (one female fly). Validation spans 164 testable predictions, 150 consistent (91%), or 49 of 58 (84%) excluding the split-GAL4 screen. Per my read of SI Table 10, Supp Table 3 lists 106 SEZ cell types screened by optogenetic activation with behavioural PER fractions (values 0 to 1 in steps of 0.1; the paper states n=10 flies per type). SI Table 9 has behavioural counts. Calcium imaging (Fudog/Zorro water responses; aBN1, n>=5 flies) is in figures, and its raw traces are not located.
datasets.licence: Repo: MIT (GitHub API). Edmond archive: MIT (Dataverse license field via WebFetch). Article and SI: CC BY 4.0 (PMC). The underlying FlyWire v783 data are CC BY 4.0 (Zenodo 10676866 API).
datasets.size: Verified via the git-tree API: Connectivity_783.parquet 100,804,642 B; Completeness_783.csv 3,327,347 B; 2023_03_23_connectivity_630_final.parquet 86,630,944 B; completeness_630 3,057,611 B; sez_neurons.pickle 5,114 B. Edmond archive total 4,589,380,441 B, including results.zip at 4,499,610,373 B. SI xlsx 2,539,037 B (downloaded, sha256 6922e168...b8d9). A minimal function-line subset would be about 104 MB (v783 parquet + completeness + SI), and the parquet must be downloaded whole to cut the SEZ subgraph.
datasets.use_in_m08: Second-choice function line, or a later H2/H4 transfer test (structure-generated SEZ sub-circuit, then predict which cell types drive PER). The SI tables give the experimental outcomes used for scoring.
datasets.independent_validation_value: Medium. The PER outcome per screened cell type (106 types), the sugar and water requirement silencing results, and the JO-CE vs JO-F drive onto aBN1 can be scored without fitting, apart from W_syn, which was calibrated so that sugar-GRN drive gives about 80% of maximal MN9 firing. My own check of Supp Table 3 (my analysis, not the authors'): 13 of 106 types have a PER fraction of at least 0.2. 'Predict none' scores 93 of 106 (0.877). A shortest-path-to-MN9 of 1 or less baseline scores 0.868. Model MN9 firing above 0 at 50 Hz gives TP=10, FP=3, FN=3, TN=90 (0.943). The quoted 91% is therefore inflated by negatives, and balanced metrics or AUPRC are needed.
datasets.risks: (1) Neuron annotations (GRN classes, named SEZ types) and transmitter predictions come from the same FlyWire data, so annotation circularity is high. (2) The readout is a proxy: the model predicts MN9 firing while the experiment measures proboscis extension. (3) W_syn is calibrated on MN9, and glutamate is assumed inhibitory; the authors report that flipping it raises the optogenetic false-positive rate from 1% to 16%. (4) Zero basal firing, and no neuromodulation or gap junctions (authors). (5) Many outcomes are literature-derived labels from the same lab (Shiu, Sterne et al. 2022). (6) Connectivity files exceed 5 MB and were not downloaded or inspected in Gate 1. (7) Large-scale simulation is costly; the paper uses Brian2 and multi-core CPU.
datasets.verified_how: GitHub API (MIT, tree with sizes) and raw README. Edmond Dataverse API via WebFetch (MIT, file sizes). PMC full text via WebFetch over the first 100k of 146k characters (methods, results, limitations, data/code statement); the remainder was not read. The SI xlsx (2.5 MB) was downloaded from Springer static content without login and parsed with a stdlib zip/XML script (sheet names, headers, Table 10 totals, Table 3 base rates). PMC file downloads sit behind a JavaScript proof-of-work challenge and were not used.

datasets.format_and_version: Feather and npy files, v783 (Zenodo 10676866, published 2024-06-02)
datasets.n_neurons_and_synapses: Zenodo description: about 130 million synapses in flywire_synapses_783.feather. Neuron count not read.
datasets.units_of_replication: One individual. Left and right hemispheres give within-animal pseudo-replicates. A second individual for the optic lobe is the male MAOL/MCNS from Janelia (see separate entry).

datasets.independent_validation_value: Structure only. Cross-individual type-to-type connectivity and offsets for T4 inputs. No activity.

datasets.name: Larval Drosophila whole-brain connectome (Winding et al. 2023)
datasets.organism: Drosophila melanogaster (first-instar larva, about 6 h old, female)
datasets.primary_citation: Winding M et al. The connectome of an insect brain. Science 379(6636):eadd9330 (2023), doi:10.1126/science.add9330, PMC7614541
datasets.format_and_version: Supplementary Data S1 (.zip), S2-S4 (.csv), Supplementary Material (.pdf); CATMAID 'L1 Larval CNS' at virtualflybrain
datasets.n_neurons_and_synapses: 3,016 neurons (2,536 brain neurons and 480 input neurons) and about 548,000 synapses. The clusters were defined from this same connectome, so annotation circularity is high. Access issues: PMC file downloads trigger a JavaScript proof-of-work bot challenge (not bypassed), science.org returned 403, and Europe PMC's supplementaryFiles endpoint returns a zip without a stated size.
datasets.verified_how: PMC full text via WebFetch in two passes (0-200k of 203k characters): methods, results, limitations and data statement. PMC HTML scanned for supplementary links and sizes. HEAD checks on PMC and Europe PMC. Zenodo and GitHub APIs for code licences and sizes.

read:fly_function_data.recommended_minimal_subset: Recommendation for the function line: the T4 ON-motion direction-selective circuit. Inputs Mi1(+), Tm3(+), Mi4(-), Mi9(-), C3(-) and CT1(M10)(-) feed T4a-d, which receive lamina drive. Structure comes from the flyvis FIB-25/FIB-19 consensus connectome; held-out function comes from the Groschner et al. 2022 in vivo patch-clamp data. Minimal legal subset, total 26,900,670 B (about 26.9 MB), all openly downloadable without login: (1) flyvis/connectome/fib25-fib19_v2.2.json, 618,148 B, MIT; (2) flyvis/utils/groundtruth_utils.py, 10,004 B, MIT, holding literature labels for development only; (3) from Edmond doi:10.17617/3.8G (CC BY 4.0): fig3_Mi1.npy 3,072,128; fig3_Tm3.npy 1,536,128; fig3_Mi4.npy 2,432,128; fig3_Mi9.npy 3,712,128; fig3_C3.npy 2,048,128; fig3_T4v.npy 8,448,128 (33 cells x ON/OFF x PD/ND x 8 s at 1 kHz); fig4_T4_vm_gfp.npy 3,168,128 (33 cells); fig4_T4_vm_gluclarnai.npy 1,440,128 (15 cells, perturbation); fig3.ipynb 263,853; fig4.ipynb 150,817; readme.txt 824. Optional additions: fig1e_receptive_fields.npy, 22,334,048 B (T4 spatiotemporal RFs, 46 cells; brings the total to about 49.2 MB); the Lappalainen Supplementary Data zip, 26,522,689 B (DMN prediction catalogue as a prior-art baseline); and, for a cross-individual structure check after freezing, MAOL connectome-weights primary-only, 116,552,210 B (data licence still to be confirmed). Validation protocol: fix structure-derived inputs, signs and offsets, and either use generic dynamics or fit dynamics only on input-cell traces. Then, without touching T4 data, predict the T4 PD/ND and ON/OFF responses and DSI, the time-course correlation, the RF structure, and the effect of removing glutamatergic inhibition, compared with the measured GluCl-alpha RNAi change. Baselines: Groschner's published conductance model (a reproduction), the flyvis DMN predictions, a sign-propagation baseline, shuffled offsets and shuffled signs. Several files exceed the Gate-1 5 MB limit (fig3_T4v is 8.4 MB), so in Gate 1 I read only their 256-byte npy headers by range request. Do not load fig1d_receptive_fields.npy: it is a pickled object. Status: not BLOCKED. Because of the leakage risks recorded in the dataset entries, any agreement with the known mechanism counts as reproduction unless it beats the controls.
blocked_items: neuPrint (hemibrain:v1.2.1, manc:v1.2.1, optic-lobe, MCNS) needs a Google login and a personal auth token. Sources: the Scheffer 2020 data statement ('Login is via any Google account') and neuprint-python quickstart.rst. Not used.

FlyWire Codex downloads (codex.flywire.ai/api/download) need an api_token from the user's account page (Codex FAQ). Not used. The open alternative is Zenodo 10676866 (CC BY 4.0), but those files are 852 MB to 9.5 GB.

flyvis pretrained models (results_pretrained_models.zip, results_umap_and_clustering.zip) download via the Google Drive API with an API key hard-coded in flyvis_cli/download_pretrained_models.py. I did not run it, because that would mean using a credential. Zip sizes unverified; the user should decide.

PMC supplementary file downloads (Winding Data S1-S4, Shiu SI via PMC) are served behind a JavaScript proof-of-work bot challenge. I did not bypass it. The Shiu SI came from Springer static-content instead; Winding S1 contents remain unverified.

science.org returned HTTP 403 for Winding 2023, so the Data S1-S4 descriptions are unverified. The nature.com article pages redirect to the idp.nature.com cookie and authorization flow, which I did not follow; I used PMC full texts instead.

Not downloaded because each file exceeds the Gate-1 5 MB limit: Shiu Connectivity_783.parquet (100,804,642 B), hemibrain v1.2 compact (45,872,577 B), MANC traced-connections.csv (75,262,163 B), MAOL weights (116,552,210 B), the Lappalainen SI zip (26,522,689 B), Groschner fig3_T4v.npy (8,448,128 B) and the other npy arrays above 5 MB, and Sintel (5,627,783,629 B).
Lyu, Abbott & Maimon 2022 central-complex data are on a Dropbox shared link with no stated licence. Not accessed; licence and size unverified.
Hemibrain licence conflict: the Janelia page says CC-BY (4.0), while figshare 11676099 (v1.0 data) says CC BY-NC 4.0. Unresolved.
Groschner fig1d_receptive_fields.npy is a pickled Python object (np.load allow_pickle=True) and must not be loaded outside isolation. It is not in the minimal subset.

Unverified: whether Groschner 2022 is among Lappalainen's 26 benchmark studies; the MAOL data licence; the Sintel licence; Shiu calcium-imaging raw traces (no deposit found); and the final MANC eLife DOIs.
read:fly_function_data.summary_for_m08:
G-FUNCTION is feasible, not BLOCKED. The recommended function line is the Drosophila T4 ON-motion circuit. Its connectome is the flyvis FIB-25/FIB-19 consensus JSON (618 KB, MIT): I parsed it and found 65 types, 605 signed edges and hex offsets, with T4 inputs Mi1/Tm3 excitatory and Mi4/Mi9/C3/CT1 inhibitory. The independent function data are the Groschner et al. 2022 in vivo whole-cell recordings (Edmond doi:10.17617/3.8G, CC BY 4.0, no login). Verified array shapes: T4 33 cells x ON/OFF x PD/ND at 1 kHz; inputs Mi1 24, Tm3 12, Mi4 19, Mi9 29, C3 16; a GluCl-alpha RNAi perturbation with 15 cells; T4 receptive fields for 46 cells. The minimal subset is about 26.9 MB. A structure-generated model can be scored on T4 direction selectivity, waveforms, RFs and the RNAi effect without fitting to T4 data. The flyvis literature labels (32 polarity labels, T4/T5 DS, Maisak 2013 tuning) are coarse and well known, so they are for development only. Main risks: the mechanism is already known and was modelled by Groschner and Lappalainen, so agreement with it is a reproduction (H0-KNOWN); the Mi9 inhibitory sign is built into the connectome labels; polarity is largely predictable from sign propagation; stimuli are single-speed and inputs and T4 come from different animals.

Second choice is the Shiu 2024 feeding circuit (MIT code, CC BY 4.0 data, no login). The connectivity parquet is 100.8 MB, and the 2.5 MB SI xlsx that I downloaded and parsed holds 106 screened cell types with PER fractions plus 164 scored predictions. Only 13 of the 106 types are positive at PER of at least 0.2 (my calculation), so a 'predict none' baseline already reaches 0.877. Balanced metrics and a shortest-path baseline are therefore required. Its annotation circularity (FlyWire-derived types and transmitters) is higher than for the T4 line.

The larval connectome (Winding 2023, one larva, 3,016 neurons, about 548k synapses) and the larval MB (Eichler 2017) support G-STRUCT only. The hemibrain v1.2 compact export (45.9 MB, open, no v1.2.1 export, licence conflict between CC-BY and CC BY-NC) supports structural CX/MB work. CX and MB functional data are scattered across papers with unclear licences (e.g. Lyu 2022 on Dropbox), so they are not recommended for Gate 2. MANC (open v1.0 exports, about 75 MB) has no verified paired function data, so it is not relevant now. All neuPrint and Codex routes are login- or token-gated and blocked under the hard rules. Independent second individuals for the motion circuit exist: MAOL male optic lobe (117 MB, open, data licence unverified) and FlyWire (852 MB, CC BY 4.0). They are for post-freeze G-STRUCT checks only.

Reading depth: Lappalainen and Winding were read in full through an automated extractor. Shiu, Eichler, Groschner and Hulse were read for the first about 100k characters; Li 2020 was read only partially. Scheffer, Nern, Matsliah and Lyu 2022 were checked only for data and licence paragraphs, and MANC by title only. Scratch working files are under /tmp/claude-501/m08fly and /tmp/claude-501/m08scripts. Nothing in the repository was written.

sources.citation: Richter O, Schneidman E (2025). Building the connectome of a small brain with a simple stochastic developmental generative model. PNAS (published 18 Nov 2025). DOI 10.1073/pnas.2504913122. PMID 41252150, PMC12664000. Preprint: bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.07.01.601562.
sources.what_was_read: Full main text from the Europe PMC XML: Results, Discussion, Methods, data/software statement, reference list. SI Appendix not read.

key_findings.finding: Generative model: neurons appear at measured birth times and positions; synapse i->j forms with p = S+(type_i,type_j) * exp(-beta_t * d) per time bin, with beta_t = beta0 x measured body elongation; type-independent pruning S-. Fitted by maximum likelihood with grid search, constrained to keep the observed synapse counts per type pair. Exact edge probabilities come from a recurrence.
key_findings.numbers: 180 nerve-ring neurons; ~30K potential synapses; binarized chemical synapses, autapses ignored

key_findings.finding: Cross-individual test: trained on one adult (worm 7 of Witvliet 2021), tested on another (worm 8). Authors say this AUROC is similar to non-developmental generative models of the adult worm (their ref 23, Haber et al. 2023).
key_findings.numbers: AUROC 0.78 with 13 traditional types; ~0.81 with 8 inferred types; birth-time noise up to 50% had a very small effect

key_findings.finding: Types inferred by greedy agglomerative clustering that maximises model performance beat the traditional types: 4 inferred types match 13 traditional ones. Quantising S+ keeps accuracy.
key_findings.numbers: 9 distinct values gives AUROC 0.77 (95% of the 8-type model's 0.81); saturation at ~14 parameters, about 5-fold compression

key_findings.finding: Edge independence underestimates reciprocity. Adding a reciprocity factor gamma fixes the triad motif distribution without changing AUROC.
key_findings.numbers: ER reciprocity ~0.0036, ~4.5x below the observed value; base model ~1.7x ER; gamma=7; triad JS divergence 0.01135 -> 0.00045 bits

key_findings.finding: Development: the potential synapses were split into random halves, used across all 8 stages. Multi-epoch models (S+ differs per epoch) track density over development; a single-epoch model reaches the same adult endpoint by a different trajectory. Pruning improves likelihood.
key_findings.numbers: 20 random train/test splits; log-likelihood ratios favour multi-epoch and pruning

key_findings.finding: Inter-individual variability: the model gives higher probability to connections shared across more worms, and its probabilities correlate with synapse counts.
key_findings.numbers: 1,933 connections in one worm; 1,279 shared by 2 worms; 863 by all 3 (backbone upper bound ~45%); Pearson r=0.35 between model probability and synapse number

sources.model_or_method_spec: Inputs: cell-type labels (1, 3, 13 traditional types, or inferred types learned from connectivity), neuron birth times (Pathak 2020), 3D positions (Skuhersky 2022), body-length curve (Byerly 1976). Fitted: S+ matrix (K^2 values), S-, beta0, optional gamma, per-epoch S+. Constraint: matches the observed type-pair synapse counts. Priors: none Bayesian; the authors chose the features by hand.
sources.validation_design: Held out: (a) a second adult individual (worm 8) for adult synapse prediction; (b) a random half of potential synapses, applied to all developmental stages, for development. The stages are different isogenic individuals. Metrics: AUROC, degree distributions and per-neuron degrees within 1-2 SD, distance and birth-time histograms, triad motifs, JS divergence, log-likelihood ratio. No AUPRC reported in main text. In the main text I found no comparison against a 'copy the other worm's adjacency' baseline or against a DC-SBM with matched parameters.
stated_limitations: Developmental 'path' is built from different individuals and may not be biologically realisable
Only two developmental aspects modelled (birth by lineage, body elongation)
Model variability is probably higher than natural variability; more connectomes are needed
The true wiring rules may differ; only the predictions overlap
Inferred types come from heuristic clustering; a more compact set may exist
sources.code: https://github.com/schneidmanlab/BrainBuildingPaper (Python; GitHub API: no licence detected, so default copyright applies and reuse rights are unclear; repo size field 123,991 KB ~124 MB; last push 2025-08-14). CPU feasible: the model is small, with exact recurrences and grid search.
sources.data: Uses previously published data: Witvliet 2021 (8 nerve-ring connectomes), Cook 2019, White 1986, Varshney/Chen; birth times from Pathak 2020; positions from Skuhersky 2022. Post-processed data are said to be in the GitHub repo. No login needed for GitHub. Licence of the processed data unverified.
sources.novelty_threat_for_m08: Highest threat. It pre-empts the core M08 G-STRUCT claim of compact rules (types + birth time + distance + pruning + reciprocity) that generate C. elegans connectomes, with tests across individuals and stages (H0-KNOWN for H1-GENERATE). It also pre-empts 'few parameters / compression' claims (quantised to ~9-14 values) and 'multiple developmental epochs needed' claims. Any M08 developmental generator is at best a reproduction or extension. This is the mandatory published-model baseline for H1.
sources.gaps_m08_could_test: (1) Baselines the paper does not run in the main text: copying the other individual's adjacency, a DC-SBM or SBM with the same number of parameters, a contact-based model (Witvliet contact area at birth), a GNM matching rule, a GNN link predictor. Use AUPRC and held-out likelihood, not only AUROC. (2) A true out-of-sample type assignment: types inferred on worm 7 connectivity are themselves a connectivity-derived prior, so MDL accounting should charge for them. (3) Freeze parameters on early stages and predict later stages, or the reverse, instead of using random synapse halves that span all stages. (4) An out-of-distribution condition: the dauer connectome (Yim 2024). (5) Function: do sampled connectomes preserve function-relevant predictions (Yan 2017 control, Izquierdo-Beer klinotaxis)? (6) Whether developmental features add predictive power over non-developmental MaxEnt models; the authors themselves report similar AUROC.

sources.citation: Haber A, Wanner AA, Friedrich RW, Schneidman E (2023). The structure and function of neural connectomes are shaped by a small number of design principles. bioRxiv 10.1101/2023.03.15.532611 (v1, 15 Mar 2023; licence cc_by_nc_nd; the bioRxiv API showed no journal version).
sources.what_was_read: bioRxiv full-text HTML: abstract, Results (feature models; three species; function test), Discussion, Methods on MaxEnt models and cross-validation. Supplementary not read.

key_findings.finding: Feature-based maximum-entropy (exponential-family) generative models of connectomes for zebrafish olfactory bulb (OB), mouse L2/3 visual cortex, and C. elegans. Features include reciprocity, cell types, distance, preferential attachment, rich-club membership, and dendrite size. All 2^8=256 feature-set combinations were compared for OB.
key_findings.numbers: OB all-feature AUROC 0.79; mouse (334 L2/3 neurons, 1734 synapses) AUROC 0.88 on cross-validated data; C. elegans (279 neurons, 3520 synapses, 15 cell types, positions, birth times) AUROC 0.84 with cell type + reciprocity + distance + rich-club

key_findings.finding: Function test: for each of the 256 OB models, 500 connectomes were sampled and passed through a fixed two-step MC->IN->MC model of odor 'whitening' (from Wanner & Friedrich 2020). The chosen model matched the empirical decorrelation, including at the level of individual odor pairs. Models without reciprocity failed.
key_findings.numbers: Preprint prints the likelihood vs function-similarity correlation as 'Pearson correlation of 0.03, p-value < 10^-6' (as printed; possibly a typo)

key_findings.finding: Feature sets differ across the three systems. Cell-type-specific connectivity dominates for C. elegans; reciprocity and within-glomerulus preferential attachment dominate for OB.

sources.model_or_method_spec: MaxEnt distribution P(G) proportional to exp(sum theta_mu f_mu(G)), with features chosen from measured covariates. Fitted: Lagrange multipliers by MLE. Fixed: the feature definitions, chosen by hand. Latent features were added post hoc to fix failures (latent motor-neuron classes in the worm).
sources.validation_design: Neurons were split randomly into equal train/test subnetworks (10-fold), with test log-likelihood and AUROC. There is no held-out individual (one connectome per species). The function test reuses a fixed activity model and the stimuli in which the real connectome was characterised.
stated_limitations: Different feature subsets can define very similar distributions, so the true mechanism is not identified
Snapshots at one time point; no development
Accuracy bounded by inter-individual variability, which was not measured
Experimental validation of the features is needed
sources.code: Not verified (no code link found in the parts read).
sources.data: Zebrafish OB (Wanner & Friedrich 2020), mouse L2/3 (Dorkenwald et al.), C. elegans (Varshney/Cook). Access and licence not verified.
sources.novelty_threat_for_m08: Pre-empts 'a small number of features generate the connectome' for C. elegans and two other species (H0-KNOWN for H1), and pre-empts the first G-FUNCTION step: sampled generated connectomes reproduce a real circuit computation (zebrafish OB, not worm or fly). This is a strong non-developmental baseline (MaxEnt features) for M08.
sources.gaps_m08_could_test: No held-out individual or stage. The function check uses one fixed linear-threshold model and no perturbation or held-out stimulus split. M08 could run the same style of test in a fly circuit with independent activity or intervention data, use held-out stimuli, and compare against a copy-baseline and SBM samples.

sources.citation: Nicosia V, Vertes PE, Schafer WR, Latora V, Bullmore ET (2013). Phase transition in the economically modeled growth of a cellular nervous system. PNAS 110(19):7880-7885. DOI 10.1073/pnas.1300753110. PMC3651470.
sources.what_was_read: Full main text from the PMC HTML: Results, Discussion, Materials and Methods (equations rendered as images were not captured). SI Appendix not read.

key_findings.finding: The number of edges K grows quadratically with neuron count N before hatching and linearly after. The transition coincides with hatching.
key_findings.numbers: Hatching at 800 min post-fertilization; body length <50 um before hatching to >1 mm adult

key_findings.finding: One-parameter models compared: BA preferential attachment, binomial accelerated growth (BAG), hidden-variable accelerated growth (HAG, with hidden variable = adult degree), economical spatial growth (ESG), and economical spatiotemporal growth (ESTG: exponential distance penalty with positions rescaled by body length at birth time). Only ESTG reproduces both phases and the timing of the transition. ESTG best matches adult degree, edge-length, and efficiency distributions (symmetrised KL; SI), along-body profiles, and ganglion connectivity.
key_findings.numbers: 279 neurons; 6,393 chemical synapses, 890 gap junctions, 1,410 NMJ (NMJ excluded); undirected backbone graph

key_findings.finding: The ESG/ESTG/HAG link probability includes a hidden variable equal to each neuron's adult degree, so the adult degree distribution is built in.

sources.model_or_method_spec: Inputs: adult binary undirected connectome, neuron birth times (from Varier & Kaiser 2011), adult positions, body-length curve; positions extrapolated by uniform longitudinal expansion. Fitted: one parameter per model (p or distance scale delta), tuned by Monte Carlo and bisection to match the total edge count. Fixed: hidden variables = adult degrees.
sources.validation_design: No held-out data. Models are tuned and evaluated on the same single adult connectome. The developmental K(N) curve is derived from adult connectivity filtered by birth times, not from measured developmental connectomes.
stated_limitations: Conclusion is conditional because not all possible models were compared
A better model might add biological detail (e.g., synapse type)
Only one-parameter models; no molecular basis tested
Positions before adulthood are extrapolated
sources.data: White/Varshney adult connectome and Varier & Kaiser birth times (public, WormAtlas-derived).
sources.novelty_threat_for_m08: Pre-empts cost-topology growth rules with birth time and elongation for C. elegans (H0-KNOWN). It also warns that an 'economical growth rule' claim can embed adult topology (degree hidden variables), which is an H0-PRIOR leakage pattern.
sources.gaps_m08_could_test: Validate an ESTG-style rule against the measured developmental connectomes (Witvliet 2021) instead of birth-time-filtered adult graphs. Remove the adult-degree hidden variable and measure the loss. Score edge-level held-out likelihood.

sources.citation: Varier S, Kaiser M (2011). Neural development features: spatio-temporal development of the Caenorhabditis elegans neuronal network. PLoS Comput Biol 7(1):e1001044. DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1001044. PMC3017107.
sources.what_was_read: Abstract, Methods paragraphs (data, birth-time extraction from Sulston lineage charts, randomisation), key Results and Discussion passages.

key_findings.finding: Connected neurons tend to be born close in time; early-born neurons have higher degree; most long-range connection pairs have both neurons present by hatching. None of these patterns appears under randomisation.
key_findings.numbers: Embryonic-burst neurons make ~80% of their connections within the same phase vs 62.1% in shuffled nets; post-embryonic 46% vs 38.2%. By hatching (840 min): 73% short, 36% medium, 68% long-range pairs, vs ~52/53/51% random. ~98% of neurons with degree >30 are born before hatching vs 74% (+/-5.5) random. 2990 connection pairs. 20 random networks.

key_findings.finding: About one third of electrically coupled long-range connections are late-forming.

sources.model_or_method_spec: Statistical analysis, not a fitted generator. A 'connection pair' exists at time t if both adult-connected neurons exist. Null: shuffle neuron identities (position and birth time) while preserving the degree distribution.
sources.validation_design: Comparison against 20 identity-shuffled networks. Single adult connectome. No held-out data. No measured developmental connectomes.
stated_limitations: Connection pairs at a time do not imply that a synapse formed then
Birth times read from lineage-chart images, with a stated margin of error
sources.data: Adult connectome (White/Varshney), positions, Sulston birth times; the 'biological-networks.org' birth-time data are referenced by later work (Pavlovic 2014).
sources.novelty_threat_for_m08: Pre-empts 'birth time explains connectivity and hubs' as a discovery (H0-KNOWN). Provides the birth-time data lineage used by Nicosia 2013.
sources.gaps_m08_could_test: Test the birth-time effects on measured developmental connectomes (Witvliet) and on held-out individuals.
