key_findings.finding: Spatial growth mechanisms without preferential attachment can generate multiple interconnected clusters, and scale-free degree distributions without highly connected hubs.

sources.model_or_method_spec: Model details (distance-dependent connection probability during spatial growth) not read; unverified.
sources.validation_design: Unverified (abstract only).
stated_limitations: Not read
sources.novelty_threat_for_m08: Classic spatial or wiring-cost growth baseline (H0-KNOWN). Distance-dependent growth is not new.
sources.gaps_m08_could_test: Use as a distance-only generative baseline with matched edge count.

sources.citation: Chen BL, Hall DH, Chklovskii DB (2006). Wiring optimization can relate neuronal structure and function. PNAS 103(12):4723-4728. DOI 10.1073/pnas.0506806103. PMC1550972.
sources.what_was_read: Abstract, introduction, model section, comparison with actual layout (PMC HTML).

key_findings.finding: Minimising a quadratic wiring cost given the connectome predicts the anterior-posterior positions of most of 279 non-pharyngeal neurons. Some neurons deviate strongly; a modified cost function is proposed.
key_findings.numbers: 279 neurons; cost exponent zeta=2 (1<zeta<4 explored)

key_findings.finding: Neuron positions therefore carry substantial information about connectivity. A model that predicts edges from positions is partly circular.

sources.model_or_method_spec: Inputs: connectome (neuron-neuron and neuron-muscle), fixed sensory and muscle positions. Output: optimal neuron placement. Inverse direction relative to M08's edge generation.
sources.validation_design: Predicted vs actual positions on the same single connectome.
stated_limitations: Some neurons deviate from optimal positions; axon guidance and command-neuron functions are proposed as explanations
sources.data: WormAtlas wiring data (Chen et al. compilation).
sources.novelty_threat_for_m08: Wiring economy is known (H0-KNOWN). This is mainly a leakage warning for H0-PRIOR: positions used as generator inputs are themselves predictable from connectivity.
sources.gaps_m08_could_test: Ablate positions, or replace them with developmental-time positions, to measure how much of a distance rule's performance is circular.

sources.citation: Vertes PE, Alexander-Bloch AF, Gogtay N, Giedd JN, Rapoport JL, Bullmore ET (2012). Simple models of human brain functional networks. PNAS 109(15):5868-5873. DOI 10.1073/pnas.1111738109. PMC3326510. (Note: volume and issue are 109(15), verified via Crossref.)
sources.what_was_read: Abstract, introduction, Results (exponential decay, economical preferential attachment, economical clustering), from the PMC HTML; Methods sections only skimmed.

key_findings.finding: Distance-only models cannot jointly match modularity and efficiency. An 'economical clustering' model (power-law distance penalty x power of shared nearest neighbours) matches clustering, efficiency, modularity, and degree and distance distributions of resting-state fMRI networks.
key_findings.numbers: 140 right-hemisphere cortical regions; density 4% (range 4-16% tested); fitted eta=2.63, gamma=3.17

key_findings.finding: Parameters estimated in one healthy sample fit a second independent sample. Slightly detuned parameters reproduce networks of childhood-onset schizophrenia.
key_findings.numbers: Two groups of 20 healthy volunteers; 19 COS participants

sources.model_or_method_spec: P(i,j) proportional to d_ij^-eta x (shared neighbours)^gamma. Two parameters fitted by simulated annealing on an energy built from P-values of topological differences.
sources.validation_design: Transfer of parameters to an independent fMRI sample. Functional, not structural, networks. Evaluation on summary statistics, not edges.
stated_limitations: Functional (correlation) networks, not anatomical connections
sources.data: Human fMRI (NIMH cohort); access not checked.
sources.novelty_threat_for_m08: Origin of the distance x homophily GNM family (H0-KNOWN). Transfer of a frozen two-parameter rule to an independent sample is a prior form of H4-TRANSFER within one species and modality.
sources.gaps_m08_could_test: Move from summary-statistic fit to edge-level held-out likelihood on cellular connectomes.

sources.citation: Betzel RF, Avena-Koenigsberger A, Goni J, He Y, de Reus MA, Griffa A, Vertes PE, Misic B, Thiran JP, Hagmann P, van den Heuvel M, Zuo XN, Bullmore ET, Sporns O (2016). Generative models of the human connectome. NeuroImage 124:1054-1064. DOI 10.1016/j.neuroimage.2015.09.041. PMC4655950.
sources.what_was_read: Full main text (PMC XML): Methods (data, generative algorithm, energy, optimisation), Results on additional measures, Discussion with limitations. Appendix figures were seen only as captions.

key_findings.finding: Of 13 two-term rules (distance^eta x K^gamma, with K drawn from degree, clustering, and homophily variants), geometry + homophily (matching index) gives the lowest energy for individual DSI connectomes.
key_findings.numbers: N=40 participants; 108 right-hemisphere ROIs; density ~10%; seed of 62 edges common to all participants; M=576+/-57 edges; 2000 samples x 5 Voronoi refinement rounds

key_findings.finding: Out-of-objective checks: the matching model reproduces the subject rank order of mean clustering, modularity, path length, and efficiency, but not diameter or assortativity. Results replicated across three datasets.
key_findings.numbers: r=0.93 clustering, 0.73 modularity, 0.88 path length, 0.64 efficiency; r=0.25 diameter; r=0.05 assortativity; 380 participants in total

key_findings.finding: Distance penalty weakens with age (7-85 years), while energy increases.

sources.model_or_method_spec: Edges added one at a time with P(u,v) proportional to E(u,v)^eta x K(u,v)^gamma, starting from a consensus seed network. Energy = max of KS statistics for degree, clustering, betweenness, and edge length. Two parameters per subject.
sources.validation_design: Fit per individual. Held-out is only 'measures not in the energy'. No held-out edges. The seed network comes from consensus edges, which is a form of data reuse.
stated_limitations: Only 12-13 rules explored; others might do better
The energy function is ad hoc
Tractography has false positives and negatives
Scalability to more than ~100 nodes is unclear
Aim is compression of description, not developmental mechanism
sources.code: Not verified in text read (the Brain Connectivity Toolbox is commonly used).
sources.data: Human DSI (CHUV, HCP, NKI); access terms not checked.
sources.novelty_threat_for_m08: Canonical GNM family and the energy-based fitting protocol (H0-KNOWN). It explicitly frames generative models as compressed descriptions, so MDL-style compression claims are not new. It cites automated rule discovery (Menezes & Roth 2014).
sources.gaps_m08_could_test: Apply the matching-rule GNM at cellular resolution in C. elegans or fly as a baseline, scored on edge-level held-out likelihood rather than KS energy.

sources.citation: Akarca D, Vertes PE, Bullmore ET, the CALM team, Astle DE (2021). A generative network model of neurodevelopmental diversity in structural brain organization. Nat Commun 12:4216. DOI 10.1038/s41467-021-24430-z. PMC8270998.
sources.what_was_read: Abstract, introduction, model and validation Results, limitations paragraph, GNM Methods, statistics on spatial embedding.

key_findings.finding: Homophily (matching) GNMs give the lowest energy across 13 rules for individual child connectomes. Low-energy solutions lie in a narrow parameter window.
key_findings.numbers: N=270 children; 10,000 parameter combinations (-7<=eta,gamma<=7), then 50,000 within -3.606<=eta<=0.354, 0.212<=gamma<=0.495; energy SD 0.045 over 1000 runs; SVM 50.45% (chance) at telling simulated from observed using energy measures

key_findings.finding: Nodal spatial embedding partly emerges even though it was not in the objective.
key_findings.numbers: degree r=0.522; edge length r=0.686; betweenness r=0.304; clustering r=-0.054 (n.s.); 68 ROIs

key_findings.finding: Wiring parameters covary with cognition (PLS) and with Allen Human Brain Atlas gene expression. Key results replicated in an independent N=140 sample.

sources.model_or_method_spec: P_ij proportional to D_ij^eta x K_ij^gamma. Seed of 25 edges common to all subjects. Two parameters per subject. Energy = max KS of degree, clustering, betweenness, edge length.
sources.validation_design: Per-subject fits. Out-of-objective topography correlations. Replication cohort. No held-out edges or individuals predicted edge by edge. 'Function' is correlational (cognition PLS).
stated_limitations: Binary connections only
One rule for the whole trajectory
Gene enrichment correlational, adult post-mortem microarrays, not externally validated
Euclidean distance as cost explains only 22-24% of fibre-length variance in these cohorts

sources.data: CALM cohort MRI (access not checked); AHBA expression.
sources.novelty_threat_for_m08: Pre-empts 'individual differences explained by tiny parameter changes of one wiring rule' and 'wiring parameters relate to capability (cognition)' at macroscale (H0-KNOWN). Its link between rule and function is correlation, not construction.
sources.gaps_m08_could_test: Cellular-scale, edge-level held-out tests. A causal function link (perturbation), not correlation.

key_findings.finding: Accounting for developmental changes in brain geometry, and using transcriptional or microstructural similarity instead of topological rules, improves GNM fit.
All models struggled to capture topographical (spatial, node-identity) properties even when the topological distributions matched.
key_findings.numbers: Average correlation across individuals for topography never exceeded 0.22

sources.validation_design: Topological fit (KS-based) vs node-wise topography correlation.
stated_limitations: Stochastic models offer an incomplete account of connectome organization

sources.gaps_m08_could_test: Report node-identity and edge-level metrics (AUPRC, held-out likelihood, per-neuron degree error), not only distribution matching.

sources.citation: Kovacs IA, Barabasi DL, Barabasi AL (2020). Uncovering the genetic blueprint of the C. elegans nervous system. PNAS 117(52):33570-33577. DOI 10.1073/pnas.2009093117. PMC7777131.
sources.what_was_read: Full main text (PMC HTML): connectome model, spatial connectome model (SCM), innexin results, Discussion, Methods (ridge regression, subgraph randomisation), data/code statement. SI not read.

key_findings.finding: Connectome model B = X O X^T (X = neuron x label expression; O = label-label rule matrix). Inference is ill-conditioned, so the authors use ridge (Frobenius) parsimony. The spatial version restricts to neuron pairs in physical contact by vectorising (b' = K' o, with K = X kron X).

Applied to gap junctions with innexin expression: 19 significant innexin-innexin rules (z>2), of which 5 have prior experimental support. The paper also gives specific knockdown predictions, e.g., AINR-ASGL and AINL-ASGR coded solely by che-7-inx-17.
key_findings.numbers: 185 anterior neurons; 5,592 contacting pairs (~33% of pairs); 601 form GJs; expression data for 18 of 25 innexins; alpha=0.215 (GCV); 5/19 supported, p~1e-5

key_findings.finding: Rule significance is assessed with a maximum-entropy, degree-preserving randomisation constrained to contacts.

sources.model_or_method_spec: Inputs: binary innexin expression (curated), GJ connectome (Cook 2019 and a second reconstruction), contactome (Brittin et al.; wormwiring.org). Fitted: O by ridge regression with alpha chosen by generalised cross-validation. Prior: restriction to innexin genes chosen by the authors to limit overfitting.
sources.validation_design: Robustness across two connectome reconstructions. Literature agreement for 5 rules. No held-out edges or individuals. No experimental test performed.
stated_limitations: Expression data incomplete and zero-enriched; one third of neurons have no reported innexin
Resolution limited to neuron classes
Predictions sensitive to noise and threshold
Many innexin knockouts are lethal
Chemical synapses not addressed in main text
sources.code: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.4027588 ('kpisti/SCM v1.0', one zip of 111,833 bytes; Zenodo licence field 'other-open'); the underlying GitHub kpisti/SCM shows GPL-3.0 (C++).
sources.data: WormWiring contactome and connectomes, CeNGEN-era innexin expression (Bhattacharya 2019). Public, no login. Processed data in SI and Zenodo.
sources.novelty_threat_for_m08: Pre-empts gene-label-based compact wiring rules for C. elegans gap junctions (H0-KNOWN for H1). It is the published genetic-rule baseline. Its rule matrix O is a low-parameter 'program' with perturbation predictions (H2-like, untested).
sources.gaps_m08_could_test: Held-out edge or individual evaluation of SCM (Qiao 2024 reports AUC ~0.64). Test the knockdown predictions against published mutant connectivity if any exists. Combine expression labels with Richter-style development.

sources.citation: Barabasi DL, Barabasi AL (2020). A genetic model of the connectome. Neuron 105(3):435-445.e5. DOI 10.1016/j.neuron.2019.10.031. PMC7007360 (author manuscript).
sources.what_was_read: Full main text of the author manuscript (NCBI efetch XML): Results, Discussion, STAR Methods headings, data/code statement.

key_findings.finding: Selective genetic operators predict biclique motifs. The C. elegans connectome has large, highly overrepresented maximal bicliques against degree-preserving nulls.
key_findings.numbers: 9,431 maximal bicliques in 182 motif types; 98 of 182 overrepresented (Z>3.4); 3x6 bicliques: 173 observed vs 0.91+/-1.21 random (Z=142); 94.6% of synapses lie in at least one significant biclique; 1,000 randomised networks

key_findings.finding: Neurons in source and destination sets share expression, lineage, class, neurotransmitter, and type more than expected. An example operator predicts 189 links, of which 31 are present; contact data explain many of the missing ones.
key_findings.numbers: 935 genes x 279 neurons (WormBase)

key_findings.finding: Significant bicliques also appear in Ciona CNS and the Drosophila larval olfactory circuit. Spatial-proximity and canonical network models do not reproduce the bicliques.
key_findings.numbers: Ciona N=205, L=2,974; Drosophila larva olfactory N=387, L=3,690

sources.model_or_method_spec: Binary TF-barcode identity; operators connect source label sets to destination label sets; maximal biclique enumeration (MBEA); Maslov-Sneppen nulls.
sources.validation_design: Motif enrichment vs degree-preserving nulls. Expression-similarity tests. No held-out prediction. No experiments.
stated_limitations: Expression data cover <5% of genes
Operators define only genetic potential; spatial routing and activity-dependent pruning are needed
Mammalian application requires development-time measurements
sources.code: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.2699419 (MATLAB, 'bdanubius/ConnectomeModel v0.2', zip 13,148 bytes; Zenodo licence 'other-open'); GitHub bdanubius/ConnectomeModel shows MIT.
sources.data: Public C. elegans connectomes and WormBase expression; Ciona (Ryan 2016); Drosophila larva olfactory (Berck 2016, Eichler 2017).
sources.novelty_threat_for_m08: Pre-empts 'label-based operators generate connectome motifs' and cross-species motif statistics (H0-KNOWN). Shows motif enrichment is not evidence of a discovered law unless nulls and held-out tests are used.
sources.gaps_m08_could_test: Use biclique and operator models as a generator baseline with held-out likelihood.

sources.citation: Qiao M (2024). Deciphering the genetic code of neuronal type connectivity through bilinear modeling. eLife, DOI 10.7554/eLife.91532. PMC11164534.
sources.what_was_read: Abstract and C. elegans comparison passages (Europe PMC XML).

key_findings.finding: A bilinear (recommender-style) model maps pre- and postsynaptic expression into a latent space whose products reconstruct connectivity. On C. elegans gap junctions from innexins it performs comparably to, or slightly better than, SCM. It also recovers bipolar-to-RGC motifs in mouse retina.
key_findings.numbers: ROC-AUC approximately 0.64 for both models on C. elegans GJ reconstruction; 2 latent dimensions chosen by cross-validation for retina

sources.model_or_method_spec: Connectivity approximated by (X_pre A)(X_post B)^T, with A and B learned and low rank.
sources.validation_design: Reconstruction AUC on the same data for C. elegans. Cross-validation for latent dimension on retina.
stated_limitations: Modest AUC shows the difficulty of predicting electrical synapse specificity from innexin expression alone
sources.data: C. elegans innexin data (as in Kovacs 2020); mouse retina scRNA-seq and connectivity.
sources.novelty_threat_for_m08: Pre-empts low-rank gene-to-connectivity rules (H0-KNOWN) and gives a quantitative ceiling for genetic-label baselines on worm GJs (~0.64 AUC).
sources.gaps_m08_could_test: A genetic baseline for chemical synapses with CeNGEN expression, evaluated on held-out individuals.

sources.citation: Pavlovic DM, Vertes PE, Bullmore ET, Schafer WR, Nichols TE (2014). Stochastic blockmodeling of the modules and core of the Caenorhabditis elegans connectome. PLoS ONE 9(7):e97584. DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0097584. PMC4079667.
sources.what_was_read: Main text: Data, Methods outline, generative-model results, practical considerations, Discussion (PMC XML).

key_findings.finding: An Erdos-Renyi Mixture Model (SBM) finds 9 blocks, including a 2-block core of command interneurons. It explains more variance in biological covariates (location, distance, birth time) than Louvain or Spectral clustering, and is preferred by AIC.
key_findings.numbers: 279 neurons; 2287 undirected binary edges; Block 6 mean degree 74.23; 186 s runtime vs 0.07 s Louvain

key_findings.finding: As a generator, the SBM fits the degree distribution but underestimates clustering, because edges are independent.

key_findings.finding: Genetic programming searches over generator programs w(i,j) (arithmetic, exp, log, conditionals, affinity function over node ids, degrees, and random-walk distances). Fitness is the worst dissimilarity ratio vs 30 ER nets (degree, PageRank, distances, triads). Program length serves as an upper bound on Kolmogorov complexity (Occam).
The method rediscovers planted generators and finds compact generators for 7 real networks, including the C. elegans neural network. Runs converge on similar generators.
key_findings.numbers: Correct recovery 97.3% (preferential attachment) and 94% (ER); exact bloat-free solutions 92.7% and 76.7%; 30 networks per size; 30 evolutionary runs per target; anti-bloat tolerance tuned once on C. elegans (5-15%)

key_findings.finding: A small 'g-network' maps binary pre/post neuron labels to weights of a phenotype network. Training alternates p-network task learning with g-network compression (Lamarckian-style). This gives high innate (untrained) performance at large compression.
key_findings.numbers: MNIST p-net ~6x10^5 params; GN30 ~2x10^3 params: 322-fold, 94% innate; GN5: 1,038-fold, 79%; shuffled weights: chance

key_findings.finding: Transfer is mixed. MNIST to F-MNIST shows no benefit. CIFAR-10 to SVHN with g-network transfer matches direct transfer with 92x fewer parameters, and is faster for lower layers.
key_findings.numbers: CIFAR-10 GN50 92-fold, 76% innate vs 89% trained; layer-1 50% performance in ~3.2 vs 4.8 epochs

key_findings.finding: RL: BeamRider innate performance stays excellent up to ~3,500-fold compression. On HalfCheetah, 4.9-fold compression avoids reward hacking and adapts faster to +50% gravity than direct transfer.

read:generative.summary_for_m08:
PRIOR-ART VERDICT FOR GATE 1 (the generative-rules map). The core M08 G-STRUCT idea has already been published. That idea is compact, interpretable rules (cell type x distance x birth time x pruning, plus reciprocity) that generate the C. elegans connectome and are tested on another individual and across development. Richter & Schneidman 2025 (PNAS; full text read) fitted their rule on one adult worm and tested on a second: AUROC 0.78 with 13 types, ~0.81 with 8 inferred types, and ~0.77 after compressing to ~9-14 parameter values. The model needed multiple developmental epochs and pruning to follow the developmental path. A reciprocity factor (gamma=7) fixed the triad motifs. Haber et al. 2023 (bioRxiv) built non-developmental maximum-entropy feature models and reached AUROC 0.84 for C. elegans on cross-validated subnetworks. Richter themselves say their developmental model is about as accurate as these models. Haber et al. also showed that connectomes sampled from the generative model reproduce a real circuit computation (zebrafish olfactory bulb decorrelation), which is a first G-FUNCTION step. Automated discovery of generator programs, scored by program length, was done on C. elegans by Menezes & Roth 2014 using genetic programming. Bayesian inference of wiring-rule parameters is Boelts et al. 2023 (SBI). Gene-label rules are Kovacs, Barabasi & Barabasi 2020 (SCM: 19 innexin rules, 5 with literature support) and Barabasi & Barabasi 2020 (biclique operators). The bilinear follow-up (Qiao 2024) reports only ~0.64 AUC on worm gap junctions. Cost/topology growth models on C. elegans are Nicosia 2013 (ESTG, whose hidden variable is the adult degree, a leakage pattern), Varier & Kaiser 2011 and Kaiser & Hilgetag 2004. Human GNMs (Vertes 2012, Betzel 2016, Akarca 2021) use distance x homophily, with 1-2 parameters fitted per individual. Oldham 2022 showed that all these models fail at node-level topography (correlation <=0.22). On the construction side (H3), genomic-bottleneck, GEM, NDP, NEAT, CPPN/HyperNEAT, WANN, NAS, RandWire, seRNN and the stochastic-type-wiring preprint already cover 'compact genome or rule -> capable network'. All of these work at ANN level and none was validated against biology.

WHAT IS THEREFORE NOT NOVEL (H0-KNOWN): 'a few features or types generate the worm connectome'; 'inferred types beat textbook types'; 'compression to ~10 parameters'; 'birth time / elongation explains growth phases'; 'homophily plus distance'; 'genetic label operators'; 'motif enrichment'; 'compact genome yields innate capability'; 'developmental program grows a functional net'.

MANDATORY BASELINES FOR H1, to run under the same splits and metrics (held-out log-likelihood and AUPRC first, AUROC second, plus node-level degree error). First, ER and degree-preserving or configuration nulls. Second, a directed DC-SBM or SBM, with blocks learned on the training individual. Third, a re-implementation of Richter's P(G|theta): their code has no licence, so re-implement from the paper. Fourth, MaxEnt feature models in the style of Haber. Fifth, contact-at-birth or contactome models (Witvliet 2021 shows contact area predicts new connections). Sixth, the GNM matching rule. Seventh, SCM or bilinear genetic models. Eighth, a GNN link predictor (NCPNet-like) trained on one individual. Ninth, symbolic-regression rule search (Menezes-Roth) and CPPN as indirect-encoding baselines. Tenth, and most important, the trivial 'copy another individual's adjacency (or its edge weights)' baseline, which I did not find reported in Richter's main text. Noise ceilings: Witvliet reports ~43% of worm connections are variable. Richter reports a backbone of 863/1933 (~45%) across 3 worms. In the fly, Schlegel 2024 reports that 53% of hemibrain edges reappear in FlyWire, cross-brain edge-weight r=0.8, and ~99% persistence for edges above 2.6% input weight (or 31 synapses). Metrics should be stratified by stable vs variable edges.

LEAKAGE (H0-PRIOR) PATTERNS SEEN IN PRIOR WORK: adult-degree hidden variables (Nicosia); consensus seed networks (Betzel, Akarca); types inferred from the target connectivity (Richter, Jonas-Kording); random synapse halves shared across all stages (Richter's developmental test); positions that are themselves predictable from connectivity (Chen 2006 wiring optimisation); within-network edge masking (NCPNet, Jonas-Kording). The knowledge budget and MDL accounting must charge for each of these.

FUNCTION AND PERTURBATION PRECEDENTS (G-FUNCTION, H2): Yan 2017 used control theory on the worm connectome to predict locomotion-relevant neurons (PDB, DD04/05) and confirmed them by laser ablation. Izquierdo & Beer 2013 evolved parameters on a connectome-derived klinotaxis circuit and got a degenerate ensemble. Langen 2015 found three developmental rules for fly neural superposition, supported by an equator natural experiment. Haber 2023 is the zebrafish OB precedent. Shiu 2024 and Lappalainen 2024 (from the brief, not reviewed here) cover the fly side.

OPEN GAPS M08 COULD LEGITIMATELY TEST (my inference):
(a) Compare frozen developmental rules learned on early stages with later stages, without random-halves leakage, and against the copy-baseline and DC-SBM at matched parameters, with MDL that includes inferred types.
(b) Use the dauer connectome (Yim 2024, Nat Commun 15:1546) or the Cook 2019 adults as out-of-condition or held-out individuals.
(c) Test whether generator-sampled connectomes preserve independent functional predictions: Yan-style control predictions, klinotaxis evolvability, or for the fly, a small circuit with activity data, trained on FlyWire-left and tested on FlyWire-right and hemibrain.
(d) For H3, use biology-learned rules as the prior for construction, and compare with ER/WS/BA generators (RandWire), NEAT/HyperNEAT, a genomic-bottleneck g-network and direct training at matched budget.
My searches found no prior work combining biology-learned rules, capability-constrained construction and biological validation. This absence is not proven.

H4: within-species transfer of frozen rules has precedents (Vertes 2012 to an independent sample; Akarca replication; Pedigo's hemisphere comparisons). Cross-species statements exist only as statistics (biclique enrichment across species in Barabasi 2020; the exponential distance rule in fly in Pentek 2024). Mission 08 must not claim cross-species laws.
